## §E13.26 — R1 correction receipt, and the second vertical fixture the proposal produced on itself

**The decisive result of the first independent review of Output 2: the proposal authored the mechanism that prevents self-divergence and then reproduced self-divergence inside its own landing commit.** That is not an embarrassment to bury; it is the most valuable evidence this arc has generated, and it becomes a **second frozen fixture** alongside `AB-08`.

Not *"the surfaces were fixed."* **Every current Output-2 assertion of a derived value must either be the owning source, resolve to it, or be a pinned quotation.** A future checker must flag both `AO-SELF-1` episodes — `ee1fa6e` and `eb8a2da` — and pass the corrected head, **differing only in being right**, which is the negative-control standard `ledger:289` sets for `AB-08`. **Four failed episodes over one defect class, by one author, under four independent reviews.** Each pass was more careful than the last; each still shipped restated derived values, and the pass that changed the *method* still shipped them. **The conclusion is not that the author must try harder — it is that a hand-restated derived value is unmaintainable at any level of diligence, which is precisely what `§E13.7` asserts and what G2 must mechanize.**

**The acceptance test for this fixture is a reader test, not a count.** Can a fresh reader who was not present state the current law — one operation, three levels, where authority originates, how effects separate from commitments, what a successor receives — **without reconstructing which revision overruled which?** A marker tally answers a different and easier question, which is why it kept getting published in place of the real one.

## §E13.27 — Dynamic assignment, run context, and the one law behind three patches *(added R2)*

`§E13.16` answers *what happens when actor B replaces actor A.* The operator's live question is **earlier and broader**: who decides B should exist, whether A continues, whether C is added, what each may see, and when one is retired. That is **dynamic execution staffing and context allocation**, and the proposal did not have it.

### §E13.27.1 — The unifying law, which makes three separate patches one rule

**`G1-FIND-61`.** R0 let a controller manufacture a substantive obligation; R1 closed that and left submission manufacturing owner duties; both are instances of a third case the operator surfaced — context pressure, cost, latency or error rate being treated as authority to change the roster. **One law:**

> **Evidence alone exercises no normative authority.** A substantive obligation, authority or assignment **resolves to a pre-existing authoritative basis** — law, contract, right, policy, role, prior commitment or attributed decision — **and enters OMNI's governed operation through its rightful gate.** An accepted deterministic policy may automate **recognition or instantiation**; it does not manufacture the underlying authority.

**The second clause is load-bearing and an earlier formulation got it backwards.** Saying *"admission is always a governed act"* without it reads as *the duty does not exist until OMNI admits it* — which is false for every obligation arising from law, contract, patient rights, professional duty, a prior commitment, a court or regulator, or operator sovereignty. **OMNI recognises, resolves, instantiates and records such duties; it does not originate them.** Making admission the origin of duty would install OMNI's intake function as a hidden sovereign over exactly the authorities the substrate exists to protect — and an unadmitted patient right would read as no right at all.

| Instance | Evidence | Rightful gate | Pre-existing basis it resolves to |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detection | Observation, candidate finding | Evidence admission → substantive obligation (`§E13.13`) | The rule, contract or duty the defect violates |
| Proposal | Submission event, preflight result | Proposal admission → decision obligations (`§E13.3`) | The owners' standing authority over the affected resources |
| Staffing | Context health, budget, error rate, uncertainty, unavailability | **Assignment decision** → holder binding (`§E13.26.2`) | The appointment authority's standing power to assign |

**There is therefore no constitutional "100-pitch rule."** A universal threshold that automatically retires an actor would make a metric into an authority — the exact collapse this law forbids. **The trigger is evidence; the assignment, continuation or retirement is a decision** by a named appointment authority or an accepted policy for that class. Existing candidate percentages in the Agent Runtime capture remain **candidate values to test, not architecture law**.

### §E13.27.2 — The layers that must not collapse

Final names and schemas remain open. The distinctions do not.

| Layer | Question |
|---|---|
| Function / seat definition | What functions exist; what may and may not each do |
| **Work-package function requirement** | Which functions does *this* operation require; which must remain independent or exclusive |
| **Actor qualification / authority constraint** | Who is eligible to hold it |
| Assignment / **holder binding with effective interval** | Who occupies it now, in what scope, over what interval |
| **Execution topology** | Which actors are serial, concurrent, parent/child, peer, reviewer, successor, integrator |
| Run and attempt | What bounded execution is occurring *(Agent Runtime)* |
| **Mission Context / run-context draw** | What did this run receive, and why |
| Claim / lease | Who currently possesses which writable surface *(Build OS)* |
| Contribution graph | Who produced what |
| Decision / acceptance | Who exercised authority |
| Credit · ownership/custody · liability | Who is recognized, who holds rights, who answers externally |

**A work package may declare, where material:** required and optional functions · which functions may be co-held · separation-of-duty and independence requirements · exclusive-writer and protected-surface constraints · allowable concurrency or overlap · token, cost, time and latency budgets · proof and termination requirements.

**Holder-binding behaviour needs equivalents for** appoint · augment · planned overlap · handoff · suspend · retire · replace · revoke · expire · vacant. **Not frozen as enum values here.**

**Retirement or replacement** ends or changes the binding **prospectively** · ends, suspends or transfers the claim · creates a new run/attempt for the successor · **preserves every prior contribution, decision and evidence item** · transfers no authority through prose or context · **does not imply the prior actor failed** · and does not make principals fungible.

**Replaceability is scoped, and this is the load-bearing limit.** Actors and runs are routinely replaceable; function holders are replaceable under assignment policy. **Principals, patients, rights holders, professional authorities and independently liable owners are not interchangeable because a new actor became available** — they change only through explicit succession, delegation or appointment. A new actor can inherit an authoring run; it cannot inherit operator authority by receiving the operator's context.

**Generic scheduler, worker, queue, fairness, backpressure and actor-selection mechanics bind to Agent Runtime and Build OS and are NOT minted here.** They are named open runtime-formulation debt in the Agent Runtime capture, tracked as `G-02` (seat transfer/suspension) and the owed Agent Work Protocol *Context Health + Controlled Handoff* amendment. **Output 2 states how architecture work uses them; it does not build a shadow home.** `[CAN→Agent Runtime · Build OS · G-02]`

**`G1-FIND-62` — independence is a claim-scoped, multi-axis *profile*; no single axis establishes or refutes it.** `§E12.2` scoped independence to a claim; this extends it to the axes on which a claim can be independent at all.

| Axis | Independent when | Current bootstrap profile — **self-assessed, not independently established** |
|---|---|---|
| **Appointment** | Author and reviewer are not appointed by the same authority | **Dependent** — one appointer |
| **Organizational / economic** | No shared employer, funder or commercial interest | **Dependent** |
| **Context / information** | Reviewer inputs are not selected by the reviewed party or a shared router | **Dependent** — a shared router selects both |
| **Evidence / source** | Conclusions rest on separately obtained sources | **Partially separated** — the reviewer reads the live repository directly, over overlapping material |
| **Method / model** | Different reasoning path, model or technique | **Unknown.** Differing model identity does **not** establish it: both receive overlapping sources, work under related instructions, and may share training-distribution and reasoning biases that no brand difference detects |
| **Decision / appeal** | The verdict is not revocable at the reviewed party's discretion, and appeal is defined | **Limited** — the verdict blocks; the delegator may withdraw the delegation; no appeal path is defined |
| **Conflict of interest** | No stake in the reviewed outcome | **Not independently established** — absence of an *observed* conflict is not an assessment |

**A concrete independence assessment is itself a claim and must carry:** the claim being assessed · the assessor · the evidence · the scope · the effective interval · unresolved dependencies · the posture per axis. **The values above are self-assessed by the reviewed party and are therefore evidence, not an assessment** — which is the same law applied to itself. Final values and assurance minima are **Output 6 / `§G1-AUTH`**.

**Common appointment establishes dependence on the appointment axis and proves nothing about the others; differing model identity proves almost nothing on its own.** Two consequences worth stating plainly. First, **the axes are not equally purchasable** — method/model independence is cheap, appointment independence requires a different appointer, and economic independence may be unobtainable inside one organization at all, which means **some assurance claims cannot be satisfied internally at any level of diligence and require an external party.** Second, the present trifecta is **valuable internal independent falsification carrying material appointment, routing and economic dependence** — it is not external independent assurance and must never be presented as such. **Required minima per axis are policy-declared by consequence class.** `[CAN→6 · independence assessment · §G1-AUTH · appointment and recusal authority]`

### §E13.27.3 — The run-context draw, and why it is `AB-08` at runtime

**`G1-FIND-63`.** Each run consumes a **purpose- and authority-scoped context draw** — the existing Agent Runtime *Mission Context* object, not a new one. The draw is a **generated projection**, which means `§E13.9`'s invalidation predicate applies to it and the proposal had never said so.

> **A successor holding a stale draw performs the wrong architecture faithfully.** That is `AB-08` in the runtime plane rather than in prose, and it is the failure mode the operator's manual relay currently prevents by hand.

The draw is therefore: **not** canonical architecture · **not** work identity · **not** a grant · **not** authority · **not** a substitute for its sources · **not** automatically durable knowledge. A successor normally receives a **newly assembled current** draw, never a cloned prior conversation.

**The receipt requires a bounded envelope, because "everything not loaded" cannot be enumerated.** An earlier draft asked for the exclusion set without bounding the candidate set, which makes the receipt either a lie about completeness or an attempt to list the universe. Seven fields, and the first and sixth are what make the rest truthful:

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| **Declared selection universe** | The bounded candidate set actually considered — routing graph, corpus, search result set, work packet |
| **Required set** | What policy says must be present for this purpose and consequence class |
| **Included set** | Exact source identities and **revisions** delivered |
| **Known material exclusions** | Deliberately withheld · deferred · rejected · unavailable — each with reason and policy basis |
| **Selection mechanism** | Router, query, policy and runtime-profile revision |
| **Unknown / unsearched posture** | What lies **outside** the declared envelope, stated as unknown rather than implied absent |
| **Reopen and challenge path** | How the recipient contests coverage or retrieves original material |

Plus: target function and actor · purpose and authority scope · context/token/cost budget · the relay or distillation applied · freshness and invalidation posture.

### §E13.27.4 — Staged disclosure is a distinct relationship, and the live fixture is this pass

The operator withheld a large speculative context packet from the authoring run, routed it to the independent review function first, and forwarded a distilled result. **That is not delegation** — and it is not one thing at all. **Three orthogonal axes, which an earlier draft fused into a single six-row table:**

**Axis 1 — work and authority relationship.** *Who is accountable, who holds custody, whose authority applies.*

| Relationship | Authority and custody |
|---|---|
| **Delegation / subagent** | Parent assigns a bounded objective; parent stays accountable; child has narrower authority |
| **Peer consultation** | One function asks another for analysis; neither owns the other |
| **Independent review** | Reviewer returns evidence or a blocking decision under a review grant |
| **Handoff / succession** | The holder of work or function changes; durable state and obligations transfer |
| **Augmentation** | A contributor joins while the original holder remains |

**Axis 2 — communication and delivery mode.** *How the payload travels.* Directed delivery · **broadcast** · relay (verbatim · excerpt · summary · synthesis · translation).

**Axis 3 — context-selection and disclosure policy.** *What the recipient is given.* Full-envelope disclosure · **staged disclosure** · blinded · sequenced · embargoed.

**These compose freely, which is why fusing them fails.** Staged disclosure can apply to a delegation, a review, a consultation or a broadcast; broadcast is a delivery mode and not a relationship; independent review can be blinded or fully disclosed. **The schema belongs to Agent Runtime and the Evidence Plane; Output 2 establishes only the distinction and the binding.**

**What staged disclosure actually buys, stated narrowly.** It can preserve **blinding and information separation** and **reduce anchoring**. It does **not** create independence — the same router that stages the disclosure is a **context-axis dependency** (`G1-FIND-62`), so a claim that staging *produces* independence contradicts the profile directly. **Its risks are structural and must be receipted:** the router can shape the author by selective disclosure · required evidence can be withheld · the distillation can flatten the source · **and the recipient cannot verify the exclusion set.** I am the author in this fixture and cannot verify what was withheld from me, which is why the receipt fields at `§E13.26.3` are obligations rather than conveniences. **A relay is evidence and never supersedes its source**, and disclosure may never withhold evidence a required authority holder needs in order to decide lawfully.

### §E13.27.5 — The orthogonal breakpoint law

**`G1-FIND-64`. Work state ⊥ holder-assignment state ⊥ run state ⊥ claim state ⊥ context-generation state. A change in one never silently advances another.** Five independent clocks — and the operator's live question, *"are we at a breakpoint for the work, or for the agent, or for both?"*, is answerable **only** because they are separable. Fuse any two and running out of context starts to look like finishing a phase.

All of these are therefore legitimate and individually representable: same work, same holder, **new run** after compaction · same work, **new holder**, newly assembled context · same holder, **new work phase** · a specialist **added** while the author remains · a reviewer added **without** transferring custody · an actor **retired** while the work stays open · a **work checkpoint** reached while the actor continues · work **split** into child packages with nobody retired · **runtime profile changed** under an attributed assignment decision.

**`solo` · `dyad` · `trifecta` · `quadfecta` are derived views over active holder bindings — never stored operating modes.** A stored mode is a duplicated projection of the binding set that drifts the moment a holder changes, and it hard-codes a participant count into a substrate whose point is that the roster varies. An operation never *becomes* a trifecta; three functions happen to be occupied.

**What an agent may and may not do about its own staffing.** It **may** report and recommend — context exhaustion approaching, a specialist is needed, fresh independent review is warranted, this work should split, this runtime profile suits the next phase poorly. It **may not** appoint its own reviewer, grant itself authority, or certify its own independence, unless an accepted policy explicitly authorizes that bounded action. This is `G1-FIND-61` turned on the actor's own roster: **the agent's report is evidence; the assignment is a decision by the appointment authority.**

**Lineage means work, function and decision lineage — not a vendor or model brand.** *"Keep the Opus lineage going"* is architecturally about preserving the authoring function's continuity and its decision history, not the model behind it. **Model continuity and model diversity are both legitimate assignment objectives recorded with the decision, and neither is universally superior** — continuity preserves accumulated framing, diversity buys method independence (`G1-FIND-62`), and which the work needs depends on whether the live risk is drift or blind spots.

### §E13.27.6 — The conversation and relay graph

The operator's question is exact: *does each seat's thread get stored, and does a successor really want to read two near-identical transcripts?* **No — and merging them would destroy the only part that matters.** Identical relayed text is not two truths; **the divergence between what each seat did with it is the signal.**

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Content unit / payload** | The exact words, artifact, excerpt or structured packet — **one logical identity, content-addressed.** This is an identity and lineage rule, **never a physical storage rule**: tenant isolation, encryption domains, sovereign custody, legal hold and offline operation may all legitimately require duplicated bytes, and **logical deduplication never collapses retention, custody, privacy or authority across those boundaries** |
| **Communication event** | Who authored or uttered that payload, when, in which thread |
| **Delivery event** | Which actor or thread **received** it, and when |
| **Relay / transformation event** | Verbatim copy · excerpt · summary · synthesis · translation · reinterpretation, **referencing a named source** |
| **Thread / conversation** | One communication carrier with its own participant context |
| **Context-inclusion event** | Which material entered a particular **run-context draw** (`§E13.27.3`) |
| **Contribution relation** | Which finding, decision, objection or artifact the event contributed to |

**This answers the operator's case directly.** One operator message delivered to two seats is **one content unit with two delivery events**, not two stored bodies. Each thread keeps its own local conversation. A reviewer's verdict relayed verbatim to the author is a **relay event referencing the source**, not a duplicate of it. **Relay order need not be round-robin** — `1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 4` is an ordinary delivery sequence and the graph carries it with no notion of turns.

**The successor receives a minimum-sufficient continuity projection**, generated over this graph and therefore invalidatable and pinned (`G1-FIND-63`). It contains: **controlling current baseline · exact current work state · unresolved obligations · decisions accepted and rejected · material divergence among contributors and reviewers · unique contributions not represented in the baseline · source references · selection coverage, exclusions and uncertainty.**

**Divergence is one compression dimension of that packet, not the packet.** A successor given only *how two seats differed* would miss the conclusion both relied on, the shared unchallenged assumption, and the current branch state. Full transcripts remain conditional forensic evidence and never default boot (`§E13.17`).

**Source precedence for continuity, and it must obey the working-packet law.** An earlier formulation said *point the successor at a committed artifact rather than a generated prompt*, which is wrong and contradicts binding law: `operator_context_and_collaboration_model.md` §2.5 states that files identified as the working packet control the immediate object **including local, uncommitted or pasted files**, and that no collaborator may reject a supplied packet merely because the repository has not caught up. The correct rule:

> **Accepted committed artifacts control accepted state. A newer, explicitly identified local or uncommitted working packet controls the active object of work and is not discarded because Git lags. A prompt, relay or summary is transport and evidence — never authority — and must pin the sources and revisions it represents.**

So a generated handoff prompt is sometimes **necessary**: when the active delta is uncommitted, when unresolved reasoning or assignments live outside the artifact, or when the successor needs the current packet rather than the last landed state. What it may never do is **silently replace** either source. And every continuity claim carries its state label — `current working packet · local/uncommitted · committed · verified-against-repo · not-yet-verified` (§2.5).

**Human contributions are first-class, and that is not a claim about authority.** They must not be lost — a one-line operator objection can redirect an arc, and a model weighting by volume would systematically under-record the operator. But **human status alone confers no general authority**: the operator may be right, wrong, drifting, hyperfocused or deliberately probing.

**And some authority classes are restricted to qualified humans.** Certain rights, duties, eligibility conditions and authority classes are reserved **by law, consent, representation, professional qualification or policy** to a patient, a natural person, a licensed professional, a legal representative or another qualified human. **Force derives from the specific authoritative basis, eligible holder, act, scope, purpose, interval and current validity — never from generic humanity and never from contribution volume.** While such a restriction applies, **an agent does not acquire the restricted authority through capability, context access, superior reasoning, or an appointment beyond the delegable scope.**

The same actor's messages therefore carry different force depending on the **act performed and the seat exercised under a valid basis**: speculation is evidence, an instruction is an assignment act, an objection is evidence or a blocking act depending on the grant, and an acceptance is a commitment. **This is `G1-FIND-61`'s fourth instance and the operator is not exempt from it** — a human's evidence no more manufactures authority than a detector's does. Treating operator input as *"assumed context"* loses the act; treating it as automatically authoritative invents one.

**Final schema and retention bind to Agent Runtime and the Evidence Plane. No Output-2 subsystem is minted.** `[CAN→Agent Runtime · Evidence Plane · G2]`

### §E13.27.7 — The realization chain, run as a falsifier

The operator's music framing was tested against the model as a **falsifier, not vocabulary**. No musical term enters OMNI. The links, tested honestly — the result is stated after the table rather than in a headline, because a headline ratio over a table is a derived value:

| Link | Covered? |
|---|---|
| logical work ≠ representation/carrier | **Yes** — Output-1 resource ⟂ revision ⟂ descriptor; carrier digest ⟂ logical-revision digest (`§E12.7.3`) |
| representation ≠ authorized profile transformation | **Routed** — Output 5 |
| authorized transformation ≠ **role-scoped execution projection** | **GAP — candidate resolution proposed at `§E13.27.3`; closes on Output-2 acceptance** |
| original realization/fixation ≠ **later independent realization of the same work** | **GAP — candidate resolution proposed below** |
| projection ≠ run/realization | **Yes** — Agent Runtime run/attempt |
| run ≠ observation/trace | **Yes** — `§E13.13`, post-R1 |
| observation ≠ accepted publication | **Yes** — candidate vs published (`§E13.9`) |
| publication ≠ local realization | **Yes** — joint effectiveness, local admission (`§E13.18`) |
| realization ≠ derivative/fork | **Yes** — `§E12.7.3` mirror/alias/fork/derivative/successor row |
| audience response ≠ commit authority | **Yes** — observation is evidence, never authority |

**Result, stated precisely rather than as a headline ratio:** of the ten links, **seven already held outright**, **one is routed** to Output 5 rather than held, and **two were genuine gaps** — the role-scoped execution projection, and later independent realization. *(An earlier draft said "eight of nine already held," which both miscounted the table and conflated held-outright with routed. A reviewer separately claimed the table held eight rows; it held nine, and now ten. Recorded because accuracy runs in both directions.)*

**`G1-FIND-65` — the second gap is the one the re-recording case exposes, and it is not a restatement of content-equality-does-not-imply-identity.** A re-recording of the same songs realizes **the same underlying work** with different performers, equipment, production and provenance; it may be sonically near-identical; it has a **different fixation identity**, different custody and different economic rights; and it is **not a derivative of the prior master.** The chain previously jumped from *realization* to *derivative/fork* and marked the distinction covered. It is not covered:

> **underlying work ⊥ original realization/fixation ⊥ later *independent* realization/fixation ⊥ release/publication ⊥ carrier/distribution copy.** A later realization may implement the same underlying work **without deriving from** the earlier realization, and may become the preferred release for a scope **without erasing** the prior realization or its rights.

**The OMNI consequence is the vendor-removal case, and that is why this is architecture rather than analogy.** Two implementations may realize the same accepted contract; **a replacement implementation may be independently produced rather than derived from the vendor implementation**; and behavioural similarity merges **neither** resource identity, provenance, custody, rights, semantic authority **nor** liability. This is the same independence structure `AB-04`'s proof ladder already governs — *second independent implementation · independently authored conformance suite · alternate consumer · portability drill* — and it is what the substrate-independence row of `§E13.20` actually requires in order to be provable.

**Requirement on the operations loop:** a change operation must be able to **create a new realization of an existing logical work** rather than mutating or superseding the prior realization. Final relation semantics (`realizes` / `embodies` / equivalent) route to **Output 3**; preferred-or-effective release resolution routes to **Output 5**.

**Rights must be scoped, not scalar.** An earlier draft added *"economic/IP ownership"* as one relation, which is itself a collapse. Any right attaches to: **an exact resource · a right type or bundle · a holder · a scope · an effective interval.** Ownership of an underlying work, ownership of a particular fixation, custody of a copy, distribution authority and recognition credit are **not one relation**. The non-collapsing set is `contribution lineage ⟂ credit ⟂ scoped rights ⟂ custody ⟂ semantic authority ⟂ accountable commitment ⟂ legal/professional liability`, and `§E13.16` states it — **not restated as a count here.** A performer's contribution confers no commit authority over the work; a custodian of a fixation owns no meaning. **Output 2 designs no IP or licensing policy;** substantive rights route to enterprise/legal architecture. `[CAN→3 · relation semantics · 5 · release resolution · enterprise/legal]`

### §E13.27.8 — Boundary for this section

**Establishes:** the distinctions and composition interfaces above. **Does not settle:** the scheduler or roster optimizer · context-health thresholds · actor-selection policy · model/provider routing · cost allocation · the final roster schema · workforce law · IP and licensing policy · Evidence Plane implementation · clinical retention · the context-router implementation. **No new artifact, no new output, no new lane, and the trifecta is not canonized as N=3** (`§E11.E`).

# §E14 — Output 3 · ARCHITECTURE GRAPH SEMANTICS — six governed objects, no sovereign graph

> **Method.** This section states **current proposed law only.** Correction narratives, rejected wording and failed candidates live in `§8` and git history, per the method change the operator imposed at Output-2 R3. **Provenance labels are the `§E7.1` legend:** `[INH]` inherited law this pass only represents · `[KND]` kind-definitional — true of what the object *is* · `[CAN→n]` candidate routed to Output *n*, recorded and **not settled**. **Per `§E12.7`: the decomposition is the proposal; every enumerated value set below is `[CAN]`.**

## §E14.0 — Assignment, inheritance and boundary

**The assignment, from live state.** `§G1-CONTRACT` row 3 requires a "relation model complete enough for a validator to reject a bad edge," with the residual "no cardinalities, inheritance rules, applicability or conflict semantics." `§G1-CONTRACT.c` row 3 requires precedence · inheritance · conflict · non-loosening · supersession · source→requirement relations. Plan `§3.1` requires the descriptor's relation set to be expressible, its three validation rules to be decidable, and the snapshot to be a "frozen resolution of every relation at `as_of`."

**The founding statement has two halves at two different force levels, and bundling them is how a candidate construction acquires constitutional standing.**

> **① INHERITED CONSTITUTIONAL INVARIANT** `[INH]` — **OMNI has no singular sovereign canonical graph. Semantic authority remains scoped, and a projection owns no source truth.**

> **② CANDIDATE OUTPUT-3 CONSTRUCTION** `[KND]` — **that invariant is realized as six governed objects: relation-type definitions, direct relation assertions, receiving-scope admission decisions, constraints and composition rules, conflict/adjudication records, and generated effective graph projections — with canonical direct assertions distributed among rightful owners and every effective graph a scoped, temporal, generated projection.**

**Four provenance classes, at four different force levels** (`GRD-036`, `G1-FIND-40`, `F-11`):

| Class | Content | Force |
|---|---|---|
| **A · GOVERNING OMNI SOURCES** | `T0-13` per-event ownership dimensions do not collapse · `T0-14` operator-neutrality · `T0-15` **projection ≠ authority** · `D0THES-DEC-033` P4/P5 own no canonical truth · `D0THES-GRD-026` payload-noun ≠ domain · `D0THES-GRD-035` **no single domain owns a cross-cutting concern** · `D0CKPT-GRD-005` (Tier-0.5, `active`) transitivity, direction, inherited-edge classification · the **4-way authority composition** (Federation admits possibility · RBAC decides capability · owning domain commits · CNS Meta enforces; *none replaces the others*) · Federation and local-admission law **at its own declared maturity** — `federation_contract.md` is `draft_for_ratification` and `C4.4 §R.16` is capture-level | **binding or canonical where the carrier says so, at the maturity the carrier declares.** Invariant ① composes these |
| **B · ACCEPTED-AS-PROPOSAL PREDECESSOR STRUCTURE** | Output 1's `AMM-C4.1` decomposition (`§7.5`, boundary `§E12.7`) · Output 2's `§E13` structures (`§7.6`, boundary `§E13.23`) — including `§E13.7`'s one-authoritative-owner-per-fact-in-scope | **accepted as G1 *proposals*.** Binding on this output as predecessor structure it may not contradict; **not doctrine**, and **their excluded content — every enumerated value set — is not accepted** (`§E12.7`) |
| **C · CANDIDATE G1 CONSTRAINTS — not accepted** | `INV-19` no globally resolved authority graph · `INV-21` observer-scoped graphs that **expose known omissions** — *the ledger's own "non-obvious half"* · `AB-16` consent/communication axes · `AB-20` compelled forgetting · and every other PRE-0 row whose acceptance condition is unmet | **proposed dispositions in an `analysis_nonbinding` ledger that *"disposes of findings; it does not adopt them by listing them."* `§E1`: rows carry proposed dispositions and nothing there is discharged or closed.** Most still **block G1** |
| **D · EXTERNAL EVIDENCE / `M-106` CORROBORATION** | `EVSRC-2026-000270` (*"own the grammar of safe coordination, not everyone's reality"*; the 6-layer shared-grammar model; the master guardrail on plurality of description; `ontology_admission_gate`; `semantic_translation_profile`; `local_concept_portability`; `living_classification`; `omitted_relation_check`) · `EVSRC-2026-000271` **`REJECT single-company-graph`** · wave-6 revalidation signal | **`omni_analysis_nonbinding`, `promote-after-reconciliation`. Confers NO force.** It **defeated the novelty** of this arc's registry proposal and **exposed a contradiction in it** — which is what evidence is for |

**Two classifications the four-way split makes possible.** **`AB-13`** is `already_present` — an **index proving the law was already located**, whose authority is the carriers it points at (`D0THES-GRD-026`, the no-god-domain doctrine). It belongs in **A by reference**, never as the law's authority. **`INV-19` and `INV-21`** are **class C**: their *substance* is separately supported in class A — decomposed authority by the 4-way composition, `D0THES-GRD-035` and `T0-13`; observer-scoped projection by `T0-15`/`DEC-033` — while **the ledger rows themselves are unaccepted candidates, and `INV-21`'s expose-known-omissions clause has no class-A carrier at all.** **Cite the governing carrier for the substance and the ledger row as corroboration; neither is "inherited accepted law."**

> **`M-106` establishes that a concept already exists in the evidence estate. It does not establish that the concept is correct, accepted, governing or universally scoped** (`G1-FIND-40`). **No surface in this carrier may state that the founding law is inherited from an `EVSRC` source.**

**What Output 3 proposes is small and is stated as such:** the six-object decomposition and its non-collapse laws, the constraint binding sites, typed composition with authority non-propagation, relation-type evolution, the conflict-as-resource split, the resolvability classes, and the rejection-ground matrix. Everything else below is inheritance made explicit at relation grain.

**What Output 3 does NOT own.** Effective-resolution algorithm → **Output 5** · change-lifecycle state model and the five change classes → **Output 4** · conformance/independence algorithms and non-loosening as a machine check → **Output 6** · per-mechanism transfer verdicts → **Output 7** · authority ontology, delegation, appointment, revocation and authority succession → **`§G1-AUTH`** · validators, schemas, encodings, generators, graph compilers → **G2** (`FWREG-021` is parked *on FAI G2 admission*, and its own blocker is that a validator written before descriptors exist "would encode the current file layout as law") · end-to-end proof → **G4** · L1 canonical coordination grammar and the domain-noun federation model → **Federation contract**, `promote-after-reconciliation` · patient death, estates, legal representation and domain survival rules → **Care + enterprise/privacy/legal** · run termination, lease release, replacement, work-package handoff → **Agent Runtime + Build OS**. **No graph database, no query language, no constraint language, no dependency-graph subsystem** (`D0CKPT-GRD-005`: *"scope to material dependencies — do not build a dependency-graph subsystem"*).

## §E14.1 — The six semantic objects

**The center of Output 3. Collapsing any two is the defect this section exists to prevent.**

| | Object | What it is | Identity | Who may write | It is NOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **`RelationTypeDefinition`** | what a predicate *means* and what constraints attach to its use | versioned, **origin-qualified**; `(defining_namespace, type_id) + type_revision` | the **semantic commit authority for that type's scope** | a registry entry · a global vocabulary · an instance |
| **2** | **`RelationAssertion`** | an attributable **direct claim** that the predicate holds between two endpoints | `assertion_id + assertion_revision` `[INH §E8.1.3]` | the **issuer** under a named authority basis | an effective edge · a permission · a commitment |
| **3** | **`AdmissionDecision`** *(an `applicability_decision`)* | a receiving scope's separate, attributed decision to admit, narrow, deny, defer or condition **an exact revision-pinned target**, whose class is declared — **type semantics ⟂ mapping ⟂ assertion instance** (`§E14.3.1`) | its own decision identity + `target_kind` + `target_revision_ref` `[INH §E12.7.2]` | the **receiving namespace** | a rewrite of the origin definition or assertion · origin truth · a registry |
| **4** | **`RelationConstraint` / `CompositionRule`** | a rule over cardinality, coexistence, incompatibility, inheritance, cycles, non-loosening, or permitted composition | its own identity + revision | **single-owner scope** → the rightful scoped authority; **mixed-owner scope** → the resolved affected-authority **decision condition** at `§E14.4.1`/`§E14.4.5`, with **no steward fallback** | a relation assertion · an instance claim |
| **5** | **`ConflictRecord`** *(challenge / adjudication)* | the governed object carrying participants, type, basis, evidence, owner, adjudicator, policy, status, **`interim_measure_decision` and its typed `interim_effect`** (a stay is one possible measure), decision, interval, reopening and lineage | its own resource identity | detection may propose; **adjudication is authority-bearing** | a state value on an edge · a boolean |
| **6** | **`EffectiveGraphProjection` / `TraversalResult`** | a derived result for a named namespace · profile · scope · temporal mode · `effective_as_of` · knowledge cutoff · policy/ruleset revision · coverage envelope | `generation_id` + pinned input manifest `[INH §E13.9]` | **no participant may hand-author it as canonical source truth**; an **authorized deterministic generator** emits it — see `§E14.1.2` | canonical truth · authority · the graph |

**The five non-collapse laws** `[KND]`:

1. **A direct assertion is not an effective edge.** Effectiveness is the **derived result of the applicability function at `§E14.3.2`** — origin validity, predicate-semantic usability, instance usability — **plus temporal, scope, constraint and interim-effect evaluation. No assertion and no admission is sufficient alone, and local objects require no admission at all** `[INH §E12.7.2]`.
2. **An effective edge is not a relation-type definition.** An instance never amends the meaning of its predicate.
3. **A path is not a source assertion.** A derived reachability result is a projection carrying its constituents; it is never citable as a direct claim.
4. **A conflict is not a boolean on an edge.** `conflicts_with` may be a relation; the *governed* conflict is object 5.
5. **A graph projection is not the canonical graph.** `T0-15` projection ≠ authority, applied at relation grain.

**Object 1 is the object the entry receipt got wrong.** A steward-owned relation registry would have made one seat the universal semantic owner — "inventing a cleaner-but-equally-totalizing ontology," which is the exact failure `EVSRC-2026-000270` was ingested to prevent. **Withdrawn.** Recorded as `G1-FIND-67`.

### §E14.1.1 — Discriminants inside the paired families

**Six semantic families, but the forms inside a family are not polymorphic by implication** `[KND]`. Each pair shares infrastructure and requires distinct discriminants, authority bases and result forms.

| Family | Forms | Discriminated by |
|---|---|---|
| **4** | `RelationConstraint` ⟂ `CompositionRule` | a **constraint** determines **admissibility or conformance** of asserted/admitted/effective relations; a **composition rule** derives **permitted path semantics**. Different authority basis (the constrained scope's owner vs `§E14.4.5`'s cross-owner basis), different result form (**admit/reject/fail-closed** vs **a derived relation or no valid composition**), different consequence |
| **6** | `EffectiveGraphProjection` ⟂ `TraversalResult` | a **projection** is a **published, scoped materialization** with publication, custody, retention and invalidation obligations; a **traversal result** is a **query- or run-scoped derivation** that may never be published at all. Both carry full lineage; they do **not** share publication, retention or lifecycle |
| **5** | `ConflictRecord`'s four moments — see `§E14.6` | **detected candidate conflict** ⟂ **attributed challenge** ⟂ **`interim_measure_decision` with a separately typed `interim_effect`** ⟂ **authority-bearing adjudication**. **A detector must not manufacture a challenge or an adjudication by emitting a finding** `[INH G1-FIND-60/-61]`, and **a stay is one possible interim measure, not the genus** |

### §E14.1.2 — Generated results are not ownerless

**"No semantic authority" does not mean "nobody is accountable"** `[KND]`. Plan §3.1's *"who may write: nobody"* is a prohibition on **hand-authoring the artifact**, not a statement that the generation and publication acts are unowned.

> **No participant may hand-author an effective projection or traversal result as canonical source truth. An authorized deterministic generator emits it under a versioned generator contract, and publication, custody, inputs, lineage and verification remain attributable.**

Six attributable facts, each with a rightful owner, all of them already the shape Output 2 established for generated artifacts `[INH §E13.7, §E13.9]`: the **generator-contract owner** · the **authorized generator** (identity + version) · the **publishing authority** for the publication act · the **operational custodian** of the published result · the **pinned inputs and lineage** (assertions, type revisions, constraint and composition-rule revisions, admission decisions, policy/ruleset revision, temporal mode and bounds) · and an **accountable verification path**. Publication changes through an atomic pointer swap, partial generation never publishes, and repeated generation failure emits a durable escalated obligation rather than retrying silently `[INH §E13.9]`.

**Why this matters at fleet scale:** an ownerless generated graph leaves nobody accountable for a wrong projection consumed estate-wide, which is the failure `§E13.7`'s four-way ownership split exists to prevent.

### §E14.1.3 — Meta-kernel termination for the Output-3 objects

**Output 1's universal M1 kernel stays closed and is NOT expanded** `[INH §E9.4`, `§E10.9]`. Its list is exactly `describes` · `carries` · `asserted_by` · `governed_by` · `supersedes_assertion`, additions require an M2 revision, and **no semantic or policy rule may be relocated into a kernel field**. Output 3 adds four object families with internal references; leaving them unclassified would reopen the recursion Output 1 terminated, or invite G2 to invent the rule.

> **Object-internal structural references are M2-declared fields of their owning object's schema.** They are **not** ordinary `RelationAssertion`s, they are **not** added to the universal kernel list, and they **may not be reified as assertions to bypass the owning object's authority, lifecycle or validation.**

| Object | Its M2-declared structural fields |
|---|---|
| `AdmissionDecision` | receiving scope · decision revision · `target_kind` · exact `target_revision_ref` · **attributed decision outcome / use effect** · conditions · effective interval · recorded time · authority basis · `decision_condition_ref` where required — see `§E14.1.4` |
| `RelationConstraint` | constrained subject / type / set references · `binding_site` · scope · **`authority_basis_ref` · `affected_authority_set_ref` · affected-authority completeness claim · `decision_condition_ref` · boundary-admission refs where the consequence crosses a boundary** |
| `CompositionRule` | ordered `input_type_revision_refs` · declared output relation or result semantics · scope · **the same five authority references** |
| `ConflictRecord` | participant `assertion_revision_refs` · detection refs · challenge refs · interim-measure refs · adjudication refs |

**Four consequences** `[KND]`:

1. **`admits`, `constrains`, `composes_to` and governed-conflict membership are structural semantics of their owning object** — never free-standing kernel assertions.
2. **`conflicts_with` may exist as an attributed candidate or detector assertion**, and it **never substitutes for a `ConflictRecord`.** A detector emitting an edge does not create a governed conflict (`§E14.6`).
3. **Ordinary non-kernel assertions *about* objects 3–5 remain permitted** under normal type, authority, admission and temporal rules — an audit note about an admission decision is an ordinary assertion. What is forbidden is *replacing* a structural field with one.
4. **The anti-bypass clause carries over verbatim:** no semantic or policy rule may be relocated into a structural field, and no structural field may be reified into an assertion to manufacture authority or reopen recursive description.

### §E14.1.4 — `permits_effective_use` has exactly one owner, and it is not a stored boolean

**The applicability function turns on `permits_effective_use`, so the record must guarantee the fact exists — and must not carry it twice** `[KND]`.

> **The authoritative fact is the attributed decision effect together with its declared conditions. `permits_effective_use` is a DERIVED predicate over that effect, its conditions, its interval and the query's scope and `as_of` — never an independently stored flag.**

**What the authoritative effect declares** `[KND]`: whether effective use is **authorized**, **authorized subject to conditions**, **forbidden**, **deferred**, or permitted **as evidence or reference only**. Value names remain `[CAN]`; the **distinction** is the law.

> **`permits_effective_use` evaluates true only where the authoritative effect authorizes effective use AND all declared conditions, scopes, intervals and temporal predicates hold. Conditional effective-use authorization satisfies it exactly while its conditions hold. Evidence- or reference-only admission, denial and deferment never satisfy it.**

**Conditionality is why this must be derived rather than stored, not a wrinkle in spite of it.** A conditional authorization is a genuine effective-use decision whose predicate is true for some scopes and `as_of` points and false for others — so no single recorded boolean can be correct for every query, and a stored flag beside the effect would be a second writable truth that drifts from it.

**One helper carries this into the applicability function, so no branch reads like a stored field** `[KND]`:

```
active_effective_use_admission(N, target_kind, target_revision, scope, as_of) :=
   ∃ decision_revision :
        active_admission_decision(receiver=N, decision_revision,
                                  target_kind, exact target_revision,
                                  scope, as_of)
    AND permits_effective_use(N, decision_revision, scope, as_of)
```

It is used wherever a foreign target must be effectively usable — `type_base_usable`, the foreign branch of `assertion_instance_usable`, and the foreign branch of `mapping_assertion_usable`. **The record carries the decision effect and its conditions; the function evaluates the predicate. Never both.**

**This follows from law already accepted, not from preference** `[INH]`: `G1-FIND-27` — *a state derivable from a relation may not also be independently assertable, or the two will drift* · `G1-FIND-51` — invalidation is a predicate, not a stored flag · `§E13.10` — a materialized projection is permitted for latency and **forbidden as a second writable truth**. **And it is forced by the physics:** a conditional admission's effective use depends on whether its conditions hold **at a given scope and `as_of`**, so a single stored boolean cannot be correct for every query. Two independently editable facts here would be the duplicated-state defect at the exact point the whole model turns.

**The authority references on families 4 are required, not decorative** `[KND]`. `§E14.4.1` and `§E14.4.5` make a cross-owner constraint or composition rule undeclarable without a resolved affected-authority set and a decision condition. **If those are not structural fields, a rule can satisfy the recorded structure while carrying no authority proof at all** — the law would be true in prose and unenforceable in the record. They are therefore M2-declared references like any other structural field, **non-reifiable** (`R39`), so the cross-owner law cannot be bypassed by omission. **Field names are G2's; their required semantic presence is Output 3's.**

**This closes the regress without minting a graph above the graph** — and without touching the accepted `§E9.4`/`§E10.9` bytes. `G1-FIND-81`.

## §E14.2 — The `RelationTypeDefinition` contract

**A relation type is an ordinary architecture resource** — Output 1's facets, identity levels, carrier separation and governance grammar apply to it unchanged `[INH]`. What is specific to a relation type is the declaration set below.

| Declares | Note |
|---|---|
| identity · defining namespace · type revision | origin-qualified; `resource identity ≠ carrier location ≠ preferred name` `[INH §E12.7.1]` |
| **accountable owner** · **semantic commit authority** | two of Output 1's four split ownership facts, not one "owner" `[INH §E13.7]` |
| subject endpoint type · object endpoint type | `ResourceRevision` **or** a named `TypedValue`; **no undeclared endpoint** `[INH §E8.1.4]` |
| direction, and the name of each side | direction is a property of the **type** `[KND]` |
| applicable scope | namespace · profile · deployment · jurisdiction · mission — an edge is **scope-qualified**, and Output 5 resolves it `[CAN→5]` |
| cardinality constraints | per `§E14.4`, with a declared **binding site** |
| composition behaviour | per `§E14.4`; a rule over **pairs**, not a boolean |
| temporal behaviour | interval semantics, bitemporality posture, and cessation/succession per `§E14.5`/`§E14.7` |
| conflict / incompatibility behaviour | which co-assertions are incompatible, and the **consequence** |
| authority requirements to assert, amend, revoke, supersede | resolved through the accepted eight-relation grammar and `§4.6`; **`§G1-AUTH` owns the ontology** `[INH]` |
| supersession lineage | explicit, never silent `[INH R8 §3.1]` |

**Ownership follows the scope of the meaning** `[KND]`, and this is the whole of Lock 1:

| Relation-type scope | Semantic commit authority |
|---|---|
| cross-cutting architecture relation types | architecture governance |
| domain-native relation types | that domain's owner |
| namespace-local relation types | the declaring namespace |

**A receiving namespace may govern a foreign relation type without changing the origin definition — through three DIFFERENT objects, not one action list** `[KND]`: an **applicability decision** over the type revision, which admits, defers, conditions or denies it (**object 3**, `§E14.3.1`) · a **`RelationMappingAssertion`** relating it to a local type (**object 2**, `§E14.3.3`) · and a **`RelationConstraint`** limiting its use (**object 4**, `§E14.4`). The **local-admission law is inherited** from `C4.4 §R.16` at its declared maturity `[INH]` — *"federated publication ≠ universal trust (locally admitted)"*, `publish → admit → use-under-grant → revoke`. Its **application to relation types is candidate synthesis** `[KND]`, **corroborated** by class-D evidence — the `L5 versioned mapping assertions` layer of the routed 6-layer model, and `ontology_admission_gate` (*"`GRD-036` applied to semantics"*). A **mapping is an assertion, not an equality**: the source anchor's own case is that a hospital "procedure" ≠ a medspa "treatment" even when mapped.

> **A catalog of relation types may be generated for discovery. The catalog owns no semantics** `[KND]` — the same rule Output 1 already applies to Backstage entities as a generated downstream consumer.

### §E14.2.2 — The architecture-plane coordination kernel: plan §3.1's relations, reconciled

**Plan §3.1 names six descriptor relations and `§G1-CONTRACT` row 3 still carries them as the object-level obligation.** After withdrawing a steward-owned registry they have no declared type home, and *"cross-cutting architecture types → architecture governance"* is a rule without a named set. **Left unnamed, a later pass either mints a registry under another name or leaves coordination predicates as local dialect — the fragmentation half of `§E14.3.1`.** They are therefore reconciled here, **not adopted verbatim** `[KND]`:

| Plan §3.1 term | Disposition |
|---|---|
| **`owns`** | **REJECTED_WITHIN_THE_CANDIDATE_MODEL as a relation type.** It is a god-predicate over four distinct facts the estate has already decomposed — **semantic commit authority ⟂ accountable ownership ⟂ stewardship/custody ⟂ canonical carrier** (`§E13.7`) — and the eight-relation governance grammar (`§E9.3`) resolves it further into steward, scoped semantic authorities, maintainers, approval policy, review requirements, integration authority, enforcement and holder register. **Adopting `owns` would regress an accepted Output-1 and Output-2 decomposition.** **And the replacement is not another edge: those governance facts are `§E9.3` bindings on the resource — effective-dated M1 data per `§E10.7` — not graph predicates.** Every use of `owns` resolves to the exact governance binding meant. `owns_definition` (`R34`) is likewise the scoped definition-ownership fact, **not** a surviving generic ownership edge |
| **`depends_on`** | **PROPOSED_AS_ARCHITECTURE_PLANE_TYPE** — an architecture-plane coordination type. Direction is supplier→consumer-sensitive per `D0CKPT-GRD-005`; `blocks_start` ⟂ `blocks_close` are distinct types over the same pair, not one edge |
| **`specializes`** | **PROPOSED_AS_ARCHITECTURE_PLANE_TYPE**, carrying the pinned-base non-loosening **declaration** of `§E14.4.4`. It may never relax an inherited prohibition; the check is validator-checkable against the pinned base, not self-enforcing |
| **`supersedes`** | **PROPOSED_AS_ARCHITECTURE_PLANE_TYPE** — an explicit typed lineage relation — `§E7.1.2`'s six-condition transaction, **never a scalar comparison**, and `superseded` remains derived rather than asserted |
| **`conforms_to`** | **PROPOSED_AS_ARCHITECTURE_PLANE_TYPE**. **Conformance *evaluation* remains Output 6**; the relation only states that conformance is claimed against a target |
| **`implemented_by`** | **PROPOSED_AS_ARCHITECTURE_PLANE_TYPE** with honest representational cardinality **`0..n`** — Output 1 already corrected the `1:n` form that implied every resource has an implementation |

**Five guards, because a named kernel is one bad sentence away from being the registry this output withdrew** `[KND]`: ① the kernel is **small, named and closed to convenience** — additions require the same governance as any relation-type definition · ② its scope is the **architecture-resource plane only**; it is **not** a universal domain ontology and confers nothing over domain-native predicates · ③ **type meaning** is architecture-governance-owned for that plane, while **individual assertions remain issued by their own rightful scoped principals** · ④ **local and federated admission still apply** — a kernel type is not automatically usable in another namespace (`§E14.3.1`) · ⑤ **generated catalogs still own no semantics.** `D0THES-GRD-035` is the live constraint: architecture governance owning a small coordination vocabulary is not architecture governance owning the cross-cutting concern. `G1-FIND-84`.

### §E14.2.1 — Relation-type evolution, and the non-reinterpretation law

**A relation-type definition can change. Nothing it does may retroactively change what an earlier assertion meant** `[KND]`.

> **Assertions pin the exact governing type revision. A later definition revision never silently reinterprets prior assertions.**

| Requirement | Statement |
|---|---|
| **exact pinning** | every assertion references the `type_revision` under which it was made; every projection and composition result pins the revisions that governed each constituent — the same discipline as `§E9.4`'s M2 pinning `[INH]` |
| **no silent reinterpretation** | a new revision governs assertions made **under it**; prior assertions remain interpreted under **their** pinned revision `[KND]` |
| **declared change posture — three independent axes, never one value** | ① **semantic compatibility** — does the revision change what the predicate *means* for the assertions in scope? ② **`required_treatment[]`** — **multi-valued**, because a revision may be semantically compatible *and* still require work: `no_action` · `revalidate` (admission or conformance re-evaluated) · `remap_or_migrate` (a representation change) · `issue_new_assertions`. ③ **supersession** — **an explicit `supersedes` relation plus effectivity, and never an independently asserted posture.** Values on ① and ② are `[CAN]`; the **requirement to declare all three** is Output 3's, and the final vocabularies are `[CAN→4]` |
| **supersession is derived, not asserted** | `superseded` may **never** be an independently assertable value on a type revision. It is derived from the `supersedes` relation and effectivity — `G1-FIND-27`: *a state derivable from a relation may not also be independently assertable, or the two will drift.* `§E8.1.1` removed `superseded` as assertable for resources; the same holds for relation-type revisions |
| **historical resolution survives** | an as-of query resolves under the definition that governed **then**, not the current one. A projection whose manifest omits the governing type revisions is not reproducible and is rejected (`R17`) |
| **lineage** | fork · merge · split · supersede, each with version-at-time and explicit predecessor linkage |

**Fork/merge/split/supersede with version-at-time is not novel** — it is the `living_classification` / `classification_lineage` shape recorded in **external evidence** (wave 5, `promote-after-Settings-reconciliation`), whose own note is that OMNI's append-only source discipline exists but *"is not applied to classifications."* **That is corroboration and a defeated novelty claim, not inherited law**, and the Settings/Catalog destination is not disturbed. Applying the shape to relation types is this pass's candidate synthesis `[KND]`.

**Why this is load-bearing rather than tidy:** at machine-scale assertion volume, a type revision that silently reinterprets prior assertions corrupts historical truth wholesale, and every reconstructed conformance claim built on those assertions becomes unsound without any event marking the change.

## §E14.3 — Direct assertion and local admission

**The `RelationAssertion`** carries, at minimum `[INH §E8.1.3, extended]`: `assertion_id` · `assertion_revision` · subject → `ResourceRevision` · predicate → **the governing `RelationTypeDefinition` revision** · object → `ResourceRevision | TypedValue` · **scope** · `effective_from`/`effective_to` · **recorded time** · issuer (namespace + seat) · **authority basis** · evidence · governing decision · `supersedes_assertion`.

**Two additions this pass makes explicit, both routed to it:** the **governing type revision** (without it, `§E14.2`'s versioning is unanswerable) and **recorded time** alongside the effective interval (`§E14.5`).

**Assertion grain — an atomic statement, inherited from accepted Output-2 structure** `[INH §E13.16 / §E13.27]`: **a `RelationAssertion` is an *atomic statement* with one issuing principal.** Many actors, signers, witnesses or dissents may participate without making the assertion a collective act. **Collective decisions about constraints, composition or conflict are separate composite acts** with their own identity, named body, decision rule and **independently attributable constituent acts** — they are objects 4 and 5, or Output-4 manifests, never a multi-principal assertion. **Participation and multiple signatures do not turn one assertion into a collective principal.** `AB-15`/`INV-17` are **class-C provenance and candidate history**, not the authority — `INV-17` still blocks G1. **Output 3 *applies* the accepted distinction at relation grain; it discharges nothing, and any residual carry closes only on Output-3 acceptance.**

**Local admission** is object 3 and is separate `[INH §E12.7.2 / `G1-FIND-46`]`. It is issued **by the receiving scope** over **an exact revision-pinned target whose class is declared** (`§E14.3.1`), and carries its own decision state, outcome and conditions, disposition and effective interval. **It never rewrites the origin definition or the origin assertion.**

```
ORIGIN TYPE DEF       A's relation-type definition revision — what the predicate MEANS
ORIGIN ASSERTION      immutable claim issued under A, pinning that type revision
        ↓ publish / mirror / custody                                          [INH C4.4 §R.16]
LOCAL DECISIONS       B's attributed, effective-dated decisions, each over an exact
                      revision-pinned target of a DECLARED class (§E14.3.1)
        ↓ derived
B'S EFFECTIVE GRAPH   the applicability function at §E14.3.2 — NOT a flat conjunction
```

**Necessary, not sufficient** `[INH]`. An origin-accepted assertion may still be unadmitted, **carry a predicate whose meaning was never admitted or mapped**, be outside the selected profile, inapplicable to the deployment or mission, **admitted only as evidence**, blocked by a constraint or interim measure, locally superseded, or contested and still effective.

**Non-admitted assertions are EXCLUDED, never deleted** `[INH]`.

### §E14.3.1 — Admission has a declared target class: semantics ⟂ mapping ⟂ instance

**Object family 3 is one family with an explicit `target_kind`, not three objects and not a registry** `[KND]`. `§E14.2` grants a receiving namespace an **applicability decision over a foreign relation type**; that power needs a target, and without one a foreign predicate's meaning can never become locally usable by the join above.

| `target_kind` | Target | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `relation_type_definition_revision` | an exact foreign `type_revision` | *may this predicate's meaning be used here at all?* |
| `relation_mapping_assertion_revision` | an exact revision of an attributed mapping assertion | *may this foreign predicate be used here **as** a named local type?* |
| `relation_assertion_revision` | an exact foreign `assertion_revision` | *may this particular claim be used here?* |

**Five rules** `[KND]`:

1. **A namespace uses its own effective type definitions under its own authority.** It does not pretend some other namespace admitted them; self-admission is not a thing.
2. **A foreign assertion may not enter a receiving scope's effective graph unless its predicate semantics are usable there AND its exact assertion revision is separately usable.** Semantic usability means **direct admission of the exact foreign type revision**, a **direct mapping to a base-usable target**, or an **explicitly authorized mapping path** — the exact branches are at **`§E14.3.2`** and **`§E14.3.3`**, which govern; **no parallel formula is stated here.** **Instance admission never implies semantic admission.**
3. **Neither a type admission nor a mapping admission rewrites the origin definition.** Origin sovereignty is unchanged; admission is the receiver's fact (`§E14.1` non-collapse 1).
4. **A mapping is an attributed, revisioned assertion and never an identity or equality claim.** The estate's own case: a hospital *procedure* is not a medspa *treatment* even when mapped. Content or behavioural similarity merges nothing (`§E12.7.1`).
5. **Origin-type supersession does not silently update a local admission** — the admission pinned a revision. Same sovereignty, and same staleness exposure, as assertion-level pinning; observability remains `[CAN→5]`.

**Retraction was the alternative and it is rejected.** Removing "admit a foreign relation type" would leave OMNI unable to state that a peer operator's predicate is *locally unusable* — which is `§E12.7.2`'s third instance of the ingress shape (external standard · customer requirement · **peer operator**) and the cross-namespace differentiator the frontier evaluation names. **The gap was a missing target, not an over-claimed power.** `G1-FIND-80`.

### §E14.3.2 — The applicability function: origin versus receiver, stated as branches

**A flat conjunction of "origin-valid ∧ admitted-semantics ∧ admitted-instance" contradicts rule 1 and is not implementable** `[KND]`. It demands a stored admission for a namespace's own types and its own assertions, which rule 1 forbids and rule 2 never required. **Left as a slogan it forces G2 to invent one of three unauthorized rules: fabricate self-admissions, silently bypass object 3 for local objects, or treat local origin state as admission — each of which alters the architecture.** The function branches on **origin versus receiver**:

**The base is non-recursive, and that is what makes default-deny composition real rather than decorative** `[KND]`. A mapping's target must be usable **without another mapping**; otherwise `F→L1→L2` evaluates as usable with no `CompositionRule`, and "chains do not compose by default" becomes a slogan sitting on a function that composes them.

```
own_effective_type(N, type_rev, scope, as_of) :=
      defining_namespace_identity(type_rev) = N
  AND type_rev is the exact effective revision under the declared temporal mode
  AND the type's scope applies to `scope`
  AND no applicable constraint or interim effect blocks its use
        -- IDENTITY, not resemblance:
        --   same name        ≠ own type
        --   same content     ≠ own type
        --   copied carrier   ≠ own type
        --   catalog entry    ≠ own type
        -- A local fork is a NEW type identity (§E12.7.1). Using a foreign
        -- assertion through that fork still needs a mapping + the assertion decision.

type_base_usable(N, type_rev, scope, as_of) :=          -- DELIBERATELY NON-RECURSIVE
      own_effective_type(N, type_rev, scope, as_of)
   OR active_effective_use_admission(N, target_kind=relation_type_definition_revision,
                                     target_revision=exact foreign type_rev,
                                     scope, as_of)                    -- §E14.1.4

predicate_semantics_usable(N, type_rev, scope, as_of) :=
      type_base_usable(N, type_rev, scope, as_of)
   OR direct_mapping_usable(N, type_rev, scope, as_of)          -- ONE hop,  §E14.3.3
   OR authorized_mapping_path_usable(N, type_rev, scope, as_of) -- CompositionRule only

assertion_instance_usable(N, assertion_rev, scope, as_of) :=
      ( issuing_namespace(assertion_rev) = N
        AND origin_valid(assertion_rev, scope, as_of)
        AND no local decision, constraint or interim measure excludes it )
        -- locally issued: no positive self-admission, and NO exemption either
   OR ( issuing_namespace(assertion_rev) ≠ N
        AND origin_valid(assertion_rev, scope, as_of)
        AND active_effective_use_admission(N, target_kind=relation_assertion_revision,
                                           target_revision=exact assertion_rev,
                                           scope, as_of) )

effective_relation(N, assertion_rev, scope, as_of) :=
      origin_valid(assertion_rev)
  AND predicate_semantics_usable(N, governing_type_rev(assertion_rev), scope, as_of)
  AND assertion_instance_usable(N, assertion_rev, scope, as_of)
  AND temporal_bounds_hold(all pinned constituents, declared mode, as_of)
  AND relation_scope_applies(scope)
  AND no applicable constraint or interim measure blocks use
```

**`permits_effective_use` is the derived predicate defined at `§E14.1.4`, evaluated over the admission's authoritative effect and conditions for this scope and `as_of` — never a stored field on the record** `[KND]`. **Admission solely as evidence or reference does not satisfy it** — an assertion may be admitted to be *read, cited or analysed* without being admitted to *hold*, which is `§E13.13`'s observation-⟂-evidence-admission split at relation grain.

**Four non-implications, stated because the conjunction only implies them and a G2 implementer should not have to notice** `[KND]`:

```
type admission       ↛  assertion admission
mapping admission    ↛  admission of the mapped assertions
assertion admission  ↛  admission of the predicate's semantics
local issuance       ↛  exemption from scope, constraints, interim measures or conformance
```

**The last one is the trap.** Rule 1 removes the *admission* requirement for local objects; it removes nothing else. A namespace's own assertion is still subject to its own constraints, its own interim measures, scope, and conformance — otherwise "self-admission is not a thing" quietly becomes "local assertions are ungoverned."

**Output 5 still owns the resolution algorithm.** This is the **applicability predicate** — what makes a relation effective at all — not precedence evaluation, profile composition, or conflict resolution between two effective relations. `G1-FIND-80`.

### §E14.3.3 — `RelationMappingAssertion`: a discriminated form, not a universal `maps_to`

**A mapping target class pointing at an assertion with no governing type is an illegal assertion under `R4`** — every `RelationAssertion` pins a `RelationTypeDefinition` revision, and nothing said what makes an assertion a *mapping*. G2 would have invented the predicate.

**No universal mapping predicate is defined** `[KND]`. **Mapping semantics are declared by the governing relation type**, because materially different mapping semantics — equivalence, narrowing, broadening, conditional translation, approximation, transformation under a named rule — carry **materially different conformance consequences**: a *narrower-than* mapping cannot carry an obligation stated over the broader type, and an *approximate* mapping cannot satisfy a gate an *equivalent* one satisfies. That is the `AB-08` warrant test for distinct types.

> **A `RelationMappingAssertion` is a discriminated FORM of `RelationAssertion` (family 2) — not a seventh family, not a mapping service, and not one predicate** `[KND]`. **What makes it a mapping is that its governing relation type explicitly declares mapping semantics.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| identity | `assertion_id` + `assertion_revision`, as any assertion |
| **subject** | the **exact source `RelationTypeDefinition` revision** |
| **object** | the **exact target `RelationTypeDefinition` revision** |
| **predicate** | the **exact revision of a relation type that explicitly declares itself a mapping semantic** — the discriminant |
| direction · scope/profile/namespace · conditions and limitations | declared |
| effective interval · recorded time | inherits `RelationAssertion` temporal semantics (`§E14.5`) |
| issuer · authority basis · evidence | as any assertion |

**Mapping-kind values remain `[CAN]`.** Output 3 requires only that the governing type *declare* mapping semantics and that its kind be explicit; it settles no vocabulary.

**Usability — one hop, to a base-usable target** `[KND]`:

```
direct_mapping_usable(N, foreign_type_rev, scope, as_of) :=
   ∃ mapping_rev :
        origin_valid(mapping_rev, scope, as_of)
    AND mapping_rev.subject = foreign_type_rev                  -- exact source revision
    AND governing_type(mapping_rev) declares MAPPING SEMANTICS  -- the discriminant
    AND type_base_usable(N, governing_type(mapping_rev), scope, as_of)
    AND mapping_assertion_usable(N, mapping_rev, scope, as_of)  -- authority law below
    AND type_base_usable(N, mapping_rev.object, scope, as_of)   -- ★ NOT predicate_semantics_usable
    AND scope, interval and declared conditions hold
```

> **The target is `type_base_usable`, never `predicate_semantics_usable`.** That single restriction is what makes the next law true instead of aspirational.

**Mapping chains do NOT compose by default** `[KND]`. `F→L1` and `L1→L2` yield no usable `F` beyond one hop unless an explicit `CompositionRule` authorizes the path:

```
authorized_mapping_path_usable(N, foreign_type_rev, scope, as_of) :=
        an applicable CompositionRule authorizes this ordered mapping path
    AND every mapping assertion on the path is usable in N
    AND every governing mapping type on the path is type_base_usable
    AND the FINAL target type is type_base_usable
    AND full path lineage is preserved (§E14.4.5)
    AND evaluation is bounded and cycle-safe
```

**No `CompositionRule`, no chain** — the same default-deny law as `§E14.4.5`, and the reason a mapping graph cannot silently become a transitive translation layer. **At machine scale this is the load-bearing guard:** cheap generated mappings compose into a de facto universal ontology precisely when the base case recurses, and cycle-safety over a recursive base is cosmetic.

### §E14.3.4 — Mapping may not become a bypass around semantic admission

**A mapping that makes foreign semantics locally usable is an applicability-bearing act, not an ordinary claim** `[KND]`. Without this, the admission gate is optional: an actor who cannot admit foreign type `F` issues a local mapping `F → L`, `L` is base-usable, and `F` becomes usable — **type admission bypassed, and the translation function becomes a hidden semantic sovereign.**

```
mapping_assertion_usable(N, mapping_rev, scope, as_of) :=
      ( issuing_namespace(mapping_rev) = N
        AND authority_basis(mapping_rev) resolves to N's authority to establish
            SEMANTIC APPLICABILITY, or to an explicitly authorized delegated
            mapping policy )
   OR active_effective_use_admission(N, target_kind=relation_mapping_assertion_revision,
                                     target_revision=exact mapping_rev,
                                     scope, as_of)
```

> **Ordinary authority to author relation assertions is insufficient.** A lower-authority mapper may still author a **candidate mapping**, **evidence**, or a **proposed translation** — none of which participates in `predicate_semantics_usable` until the required authority or an active admission exists. **A foreign mapping always requires active receiving-scope mapping admission permitting effective use.**

**Boundary.** Output 3 owns the **non-bypass law** — mapping cannot confer applicability on weaker authority than admission would require. **`§G1-AUTH` owns** the role and seat vocabulary, delegation, thresholds, the decision-condition ontology, and which policies may pre-authorize mappings. **No seat is minted here.**

> **A mapped edge is a DERIVED projection result, never a direct assertion** `[KND]`. It carries as lineage the **origin assertion**, the **mapping assertion**, and the **local target type revision**. **The origin is never rewritten**, and the mapped edge is never citable as a direct claim — non-collapse law 3 (`path ≠ source assertion`) applied to translation. **Mapping is never identity or equality** (`§E14.3.1` rule 4): a hospital *procedure* mapped to a medspa *treatment* remains two types with a recorded, attributed, revisable relationship between them. `G1-FIND-80`.

**Typed absence** `[INH §4.8 / `§E12.7.2`]`: no admission decision is `absent`, or `unknown` where even its existence cannot be established. The resolver may **project** `not_determined` as a **derived** result; it is never a stored decision state, and **`denied` requires an attributed decision that exists and says no.**

**Origin supersession does not propagate** — B pinned a revision. That is correct sovereignty and it is also how B runs stale law indefinitely, so **origin supersession must be observable to admitters** `[CAN→5]`.

**Confidence stays typed and plural** `[INH §E12.7.2]`. There is no universal confidence scalar: normative authority state ⟂ evidentiary confidence ⟂ validation result ⟂ source credibility. Clinical Memory holds the same separation one layer down — `authority` ≠ `status` (who agrees) ≠ `confidence` (the source's self-report) `[INH CM §5]`.

## §E14.4 — Constraints and typed composition

### §E14.4.1 — Every constraint declares its binding site

**A constraint is meaningless until it says what it constrains** `[KND]`. Three binding sites, never conflated:

| Binding site | Constrains |
|---|---|
| **direct** | what an issuer may assert within its own scope |
| **admitted** | what a receiving scope may admit |
| **effective** | what may hold in a resolved projection |

And every constraint declares its **scope** (namespace · profile · deployment · jurisdiction · interval), its **authority**, and its **rejection consequence**.

**Constraint authority is unilateral only inside the declaring authority's own scope** `[KND]`. This is the same insufficiency `§E14.4.5` diagnoses for composition, one object over: *"the authority owning the constrained scope"* resolves nothing when the constrained scope is not one owner's. Where a constraint **spans independently owned relation types** · **constrains endpoints owned by several domains** · **changes consequences across an operator or federation boundary** · or **touches a non-waivable right or duty**, it requires the **same explicit decision condition** as a cross-owner composition rule: every affected semantic authority, boundary admission where the consequence crosses one, independently held rights or duties (`INV-30`), and refusal treated as blocking rather than absent.

> **No architecture-steward fallback. An unresolved affected-authority set blocks the constraint from being declared** — it does not default upward, exactly as `owner_set_complete` blocks rather than defaulting `[INH §E13.8]`. `G1-FIND-83`.

### §E14.4.2 — Cardinality names its side and its site

Declare **subject-side** and **object-side** cardinality separately, each at a named binding site. `0..n` is the default only where nothing narrower is declared — Output 1 already corrected `1:n` cardinalities that wrongly implied every resource has an implementation, verifier or evidence object `[INH §E8.1.5]`.

> **Representational cardinality ⟂ conformance cardinality** `[INH §E10.5]`.
