The format may permit zero or several assertions while policy requires **exactly one currently effective admitted relation**. **Do not encode a policy requirement by making the invalid state unrecordable** — a model that cannot express the broken state it was built to measure cannot measure it, which is why `resource_steward` being declared for zero of seven real resources is diagnosable at all.

### §E14.4.3 — Exclusivity is a constraint surface, not a pairwise flag

Representable constraint forms `[CAN]`, each with subject, set, scope, binding site, authority and consequence: **at-most-one-of** a set · **exactly-one-of** a set · **requires-one-of** · **prohibited co-occurrence** · **acyclic** · **no self-loop** · **no path across a protected boundary** · **mutually exclusive within a profile or interval only**.

**Coexistence is the default; exclusivity must be declared** `[KND]`. The estate's live bound is Clinical Memory §5: *same concept, different `context_key` = coexisting active assertions, **not** a conflict* `[INH]`.

**No generic constraint language is authored here.** Output 3 establishes that a constraint has a subject, a scope, a binding site, an authority and a rejection consequence. Expression, evaluation and enforcement are Outputs 5/6 and G2.

### §E14.4.4 — Inheritance and non-loosening

Two derivation kinds, kept apart `[INH §E7.1.5]`: `specialization` **adds**; `constraint` may only add restrictions or rules to inherited content. **The accepted law is `§E8.6`'s, and it is narrower than the mechanism claim it replaced** `[INH]`:

> **A constraint relation declares a non-loosening requirement against an exact pinned predecessor. Because a `constraint` derivation may only add restrictions, a validator can reject *structural* loosening relative to that pinned base. It does NOT self-enforce because the field is present, and semantic weakening expressed in prose still requires a computable rule representation or independent review** `[CAN→6]`.

**A `specializes` edge may never relax an inherited prohibition** — and that requirement is *declared and checked*, not automatically satisfied by the derivation kind. `NC-8`'s semantic check remains open to Outputs 3+6 `[INH §7.3]`, and Clinical Memory independently carries LOOSENING/TIGHTENING semantics on `concept_version` `[INH CM §6.1]` (`G1-FIND-70`).

### §E14.4.5 — Typed composition, and the law that keeps it safe

**Composition is a rule over an ordered pair of relation types, not a boolean on one type** `[KND]`:

```
r1 ∘ r2  →  r3                     compose to a third declared type
r1 ∘ r2  →  same-type reachability derived reachability, marked derived
r1 ∘ r2  →  no valid composition   the default where no rule is declared
```

A composition rule may additionally depend on endpoint types · scope/profile · time · admission state · policy. **Absent a declared rule, no composition is valid** `[KND]`.

**Who may declare a composition rule that spans independently owned relation types** `[KND]`. *"The authority owning the constrained scope"* is sufficient only where one owner controls the whole semantic consequence, and a composition rule routinely does not: `r1` may be domain-owned and `r2` namespace-local, so the rule's consequence lands outside either owner's scope. **There is no architecture-steward fallback** — that would rebuild the universal semantic owner `§E14.1` withdrew, one level up.

> **A composition rule resolves through a decision condition over every affected semantic authority — not through a single owner and not through a default.** The basis names: **every affected relation-type semantic authority** · **cross-cutting architecture authority only where the consequence is genuinely cross-cutting** · **operator/federation admission** for any rule whose consequence crosses a boundary · **independently held rights or duties** that no majority may vote away (`INV-30`) · and **explicit treatment of refusal**, which blocks rather than being absent (`§4.5`, `G1-FIND-36`).

**Where the affected-authority set cannot be resolved, the rule is not declared** — it reports unresolved and blocks, exactly as `owner_set_complete` does `[INH §E13.8]`. **The decision-condition ontology itself is `§G1-AUTH`'s; the requirement that a composition rule have one is Output 3's** `[CAN→AUTH]`.

**Every derived path result preserves** `[KND]`: every direct assertion used · the exact path · the composition-rule identities **and revisions** · temporal and scope compatibility across the whole path · the coverage posture · and an explicit **direct-versus-derived** marker.

> ### The authority non-propagation law
> **Authority never propagates merely because a path composes** `[KND]`.
>
> `A depends_on B` and `B depends_on C` may support derived impact reachability from A to C. It does **not** make A authoritative over C, transfer C's ownership or custody, confer a right to approve C, or manufacture an approval obligation unsupported by policy. **The inherited substance is class A** — the **4-way authority composition** (*"none replaces the others"*), `D0THES-GRD-035` (no single domain owns a cross-cutting concern) and `T0-13` (per-event ownership dimensions do not collapse) — **plus accepted Output-2 `G1-FIND-50`'s policy-not-adjacency structure** `[INH]`. **`INV-19` is a class-C PRE-0 candidate that corroborates this and is not its authority** (`§E14.0`).

**No uninspected closure** `[INH D0CKPT-GRD-005]`. Transitive composition is legitimate; adding an edge to a provider without inspecting that provider's active upstream closure is the defect. Each inherited edge must be **explicitly classified**, and the classification is what discharges it — scope or vintage mismatch is grounds to suspect an inherited edge, never licence to drop it silently.

### §E14.4.6 — Do not universalize the dependency-classification vocabulary

`accepted | narrowed | rejected | pending_revalidation` is **inherited for the dependency-edge inheritance problem that owns it** `[INH D0CKPT-GRD-005]` and is **not** the universal lifecycle of every OMNI relation. Eight facets stay separate `[KND]`, each with its own owner and its own value set `[CAN]`:

issuer-side assertion decision state ⟂ receiving-scope admission **(by target class — semantics ⟂ mapping ⟂ instance)** ⟂ assertion lifecycle ⟂ **dependency-inheritance classification (scope-labelled to `D0CKPT-GRD-005`)** ⟂ validation result ⟂ **challenge ⟂ `interim_measure_decision` ⟂ typed `interim_effect`** ⟂ coverage/freshness posture ⟂ typed absence.

**The estate's only explicit edge-kind declaration fuses two of these.** `v4_pre_spine…map` §6.1 lists `blocks_start` · `blocks_close` · `downstream_consumption` · `pending_revalidation` as one set: the first three are **relation types**, the fourth is an **adjudication state**, and a fifth value was minted inline beside them. **Repair is by decomposition, not by re-derivation** — the same `F-08` correction Output 1 made four times. Recorded as `G1-FIND-68`; the fix belongs to that map's rightful writer and **is not performed here**.

## §E14.5 — Time, supersession, revocation and invalidation

**Relation bitemporality — PROPOSED RESOLUTION of the `[CAN→3]` Output 1 deliberately left open** `[KND]`: a `RelationAssertion` carries **both** an effective interval **and** a recorded time. Without recorded time, `known_as_of` and `decision_context_replay` are unanswerable over relations, and Output 2's temporal modes cannot bind.

> **Output 3 proposes this resolution. The Output-1 carry remains OPEN while Output 3 is `PROPOSED · NOT_ACCEPTED`; acceptance of Output 3 would discharge it within the accepted boundary.** `G1-FIND-72`.

**And the assertion is not the only object whose time matters.** The invalidation predicate below already pins type-definition, admission, constraint, composition-rule and conflict revisions as constituents; a pinned constituent with no temporal semantics cannot answer the mode it was pinned for. **The requirement is stated by object physics, not as one universal field set** — a projection has no normative interval to carry, and a detection event has no effectivity to declare `[KND]`:

| Object | Minimum temporal semantics |
|---|---|
| `RelationTypeDefinition` revision | recorded time **+** effective interval **for its normative meaning** |
| `RelationAssertion` revision | recorded time **+** effective interval |
| `AdmissionDecision` revision | recorded time **+** effective interval |
| `RelationConstraint` revision | recorded time **always**, **+** effective interval for **any constraint capable of changing admissibility, conformance, effective resolution, rejection or blocking**. **A purely advisory or evidentiary statement is not a consequence-bearing `RelationConstraint`** — it is evidence or analysis and belongs to those objects. |
| `RelationMappingAssertion` revision | inherits `RelationAssertion` temporal semantics — recorded time **+** effective interval |
| `CompositionRule` revision | recorded time **+** effective interval |
| `ConflictRecord` — detection, challenge | **recorded event time** *(no effectivity: neither changes force)* |
| `ConflictRecord` — interim measure, adjudication | recorded time **+** effective time or interval appropriate to the decision's effect |
| `EffectiveGraphProjection` / `TraversalResult` | generation/recorded time **+** temporal mode **+** `effective_as_of` **+** `recorded_as_of`/knowledge cutoff. **No independent normative interval** unless a separate publication decision supplies one |

> **The founding law:** **every revision or act whose force, applicability or historical interpretation can vary over time must expose enough effective-time and recorded-time semantics to answer the declared temporal question.** Where it does not, the question is not answerable and the request fails rather than returning a confident wrong answer (`R35`).

**Do not read this as a universal bitemporal record shape.** Stamping one field set over objects with different physics is the `F-08` failure — and Output 1 spent four passes removing exactly that. `G1-FIND-82`.

**The four temporal modes bind at relation grain** `[INH §E13.5]`. `historical_as_now_reconstructed(effective_as_of)` **may** use later-recorded, earlier-effective assertions; `known_as_of`, `decision_context_replay` and `evaluation_against_the_knowledge_horizon_then` **may not**. **No-hindsight binds the last three and not the first** — the relation-grain resolution Output 3 **proposes** for `G1-FIND-45`, which remains open while Output 3 is `PROPOSED · NOT_ACCEPTED`. Every graph projection declares: temporal question/mode · `effective_as_of` · `recorded_as_of` or knowledge cutoff · resolver scope and profile · whether later evidence is admissible — and because a projection is content-addressed, **mode and both bounds sit inside its input manifest** `[INH]`. **The resolution algorithm is Output 5's; C4.5 owns temporal architecture.**

**Supersession is a typed transaction, never a comparison** `[INH §E7.1.2]` — six conditions, no ordering anywhere.

**The one surviving prohibition, stated semantically over the inherited facet separation** `[INH decomposition]`:

> **A would-be superseder that does not carry binding normative effect may not supersede a predecessor that carries binding normative effect.**

**What is inherited is the separation, not an enumeration** `[INH]`: `normative_effect` (**the force a resource carries**) ⟂ `epistemic_role[]` (**how it may be used epistemically**). Output 1 stated the prohibition over the pre-split `normative_force`; R6 split that field precisely because it fused a force with an epistemic use. **The exact values of both facets remain `[CAN→3/6]` under the accepted Output-1 boundary, which holds that the facet decomposition is core and the enumerated values are not** (`§E12.7`). Stating the prohibition semantically rather than by value list is therefore both the correct provenance and the substrate-independent form.

**`epistemic_role[]` does not enter this prohibition at all.** Whether something is evidence, analysis or reference is orthogonal to whether it carries binding force. The four facts the transaction composes stay separate: **predecessor and successor normative effect** ⟂ **predecessor and successor epistemic role** ⟂ **the governing authority and decision condition** (`§4.6`, `§4.5`) ⟂ **the exact supersession policy**, which is `§E7.1.2`'s six conditions, unchanged. `G1-FIND-71`, `G1-FIND-79`.

**Revocation is prospective and erases nothing** `[INH `G1-FIND-53`]`. Ending a relation closes its interval; it does not delete the assertion, rewrite history, or remove a recorded refusal.

**Invalidation is a predicate, not a stored flag** `[INH `G1-FIND-51`]`. A projection is stale when its pinned constituents — assertions, type revisions, constraint/composition-rule revisions, admission decisions, endpoint revisions, policy/ruleset revision — no longer match what the query requires. **Determining staleness requires no write anywhere**, and an `is_stale` boolean would rebuild the duplicated state this model exists to abolish.

**Incremental invalidation is a consequence, not a mechanism** `[KND]`: because every projection pins its constituents, a change to any one of them invalidates the dependent projection **without rewriting any source assertion**.

## §E14.6 — Conflict, challenge, interim measure, adjudication and precedence references

**`conflicts_with` may be a relation. The governed conflict is object 5** `[KND]`, carrying: identity · participating assertions · conflict type · scope · detection basis · evidence · owner · adjudicating authority · governing policy · status · `interim_measure_decision` and its typed `interim_effect` · decision · effective time · reopening · resolution lineage.

**Four moments, and they do not collapse** `[KND]`. A `ConflictRecord` may carry all four over its life, but each is a separately attributable act with its own author and its own effect:

| Moment | Who | Effect on effective force |
|---|---|---|
| **detected candidate conflict** | any detector, controller or agent — **emits a candidate** | **none** |
| **attributed challenge** | a principal with standing, stating scope, basis and evidence | **none by itself** |
| **interim measure decision** | an authority competent to act pending resolution | **a separately typed `interim_effect`** — the only moment that may change force **without resolving**. **A stay is one typed interim measure, not the genus:** an interim decision may instead preserve current force, narrow scope, condition use, quarantine a dependent projection, suspend, or require further evidence. Values `[CAN]`; **the decision and its effect are two facts, and collapsing them makes every interim act a suspension** |
| **authority-bearing adjudication** | the adjudicating authority under the governing policy | **resolves**, with lineage and reopening preserved |

> **A detector must not manufacture a challenge or an adjudication by emitting a finding** `[INH G1-FIND-60/-61]` — controllers emit candidates, and evidence never manufactures an obligation, an authority or an assignment. **A challenge is not a stay**, and **a stay is not an adjudication**: collapsing the second into the third is how filing becomes deciding, and collapsing the first into the second is how a lint run becomes a dispute.

**Precedence is a reference, never an intrinsic scalar** `[KND]`. Output 3 may represent a **precedence-policy reference**, a **specific adjudication**, a **rule that one type constrains another**, or a **named decision condition** (`§4.5`). It represents **no universal source ranking and no authority score**. Output 5 evaluates effective resolution.

**Four preservation rules** `[INH]`: conflicting assertions are **all preserved** · no silent winner where policy requires review — Clinical Memory's `requires_provider_review_on_conflict` **fails closed until reconciled**, and plan §5 test 2 independently requires ambiguous or contradictory combinations to fail closed with a named owner and reason · **no deletion of the non-effective assertion** · **no silent dedup that erases history** (CM §7).

**A challenge does not change effective force** `[INH §E12.7.2]`. An accepted relation may be disputed while remaining in force; only a separate authority-bearing **stay, suspension, revocation, supersession or local non-admission** changes it. As a mutually exclusive state, `disputed` would be an architectural denial-of-service primitive.

**Clinical Memory's locked authority precedence is not a counter-example and is not importable** `[KND]`. Its eight-value `authority_rank` is a **read-view tie-break over `(patient, concept, context_key)` for competing claims about one clinical fact**. Architecture relation governance ranks nothing. Both are correct for their subjects; the statement of why they differ is what stops the next agent importing either into the other.

## §E14.7 — Federation, identity, independent realization and scoped rights

### §E14.7.1 — Resolvability classes

**"Unknown relation target fails" is not one rule.** Six classes, each with a different failure `[KND]`:

| # | Class | Rejects? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | valid externally identified endpoint, **not locally materialized** | **No** — a legitimate federated reference; downgrades coverage posture |
| 2 | known endpoint, **stale or broken locator** | **Yes** for locator resolution; the identity survives — repair the pointer, not the identity |
| 3 | **unknown endpoint identity** | **Yes** — no resolvable subject is established |
| 4 | **undeclared or invalid endpoint type** | **Yes** — semantically malformed; the type contract is violated |
| 5 | exists, **locally unadmitted** | **No** — excluded from the effective projection, never deleted |
| 6 | **uncovered / untyped prose relationship** | **No** — reports `unknown`/`partial`; never reports clean |

**Identity ⟂ locator is the load-bearing split** `[KND]`. Class 2 is a projection-verification failure, not a semantic one, and treating it as class 3 would invalidate every legitimate not-yet-materialized reference.

**Bootstrap posture** `[INH §E13.8]`: closure is required over the **descriptor-covered subgraph**; uncovered surfaces report `unknown`/`partial` and **never clean**; high-consequence classes stay blocked until covered; lower-consequence classes proceed only under a named, authority-bearing bootstrap policy with declared residual risk.

### §E14.7.2 — Realization — one relation, not two

**`realizes` is the single predicate** `[KND]`. `embodies` is withdrawn as a synonym; the estate establishes no material distinction, and Output 1's accepted set already carries `realizes_interface` as its specialization. The distinctions are carried by **endpoint type and declared facets**, not by minting near-synonyms:

`governing work / specification` ⊥ `original realization` ⊥ **later independent realization** ⊥ `derived realization` ⊥ `release / publication` ⊥ `carrier / distribution copy` ⊥ `preferred realization for a scope` `[INH `G1-FIND-65`]`.

**A later independent realization realizes the same governing work without being derived from the prior realization** `[INH]`. Behavioural equivalence merges **neither** identity, provenance, custody, scoped rights, semantic authority **nor** liability — and a validator that infers `derived_from` from behavioural or content similarity is wrong in the direction that destroys the substrate-independence proof. Preferred-realization resolution is **Output 5's**.

**Rights are separately scoped facts, never inferred** `[INH]`: `exact resource · right type or bundle · holder · scope · effective interval`. They are not inferred from `realizes`, similarity, contribution, custody or distribution. **No IP or licensing doctrine is authored here.**

### §E14.7.3 — Operational identity and alias collision

**Seven things stay separate** `[KND]`: stable entity/actor identity · operation or work identity · physical realization · function/seat · holder binding · human-facing name or alias · temporary local disambiguator.

**A name, model label, thread name, display label or seat label is never a durable identity merely because humans use it conversationally** `[INH]`. This is Identity's `handle ≠ person` law generalized: *"a phone/email handle may map to several people; resolution treats shared-handle/ambiguous-handle/typo as first-class states and **never blind-matches** a handle to one patient"* (Identity inv 9), plus AWP `L3` — **durable identity is the carrier, never the machine.**

**An operational alias is a scoped, intervalled, attributed binding** `[KND]`, carrying: **assigning namespace** · **assigning principal, actor and grant basis** · **the exact target** (identity + revision where the target is revisioned) · **scope and channel** · **effective interval** · **supersession or withdrawal** · and **anti-equivocation**. Without the issuer fields an alias binding cannot be challenged, revoked or attributed, and it becomes exactly the ungoverned display label this section exists to prevent.

**Anti-equivocation** `[KND]`, the alias-layer form of Output 1's rule that one `revision_id` may never resolve to two contents:

> **An issuer may not validly bind the same operational alias to two active targets in the same consequence-bearing scope and interval. Attempting it does not silently pick one and does not overwrite the earlier binding — it creates an explicit conflict that blocks high-consequence resolution** until disambiguated or one binding is withdrawn.

The semantic requirement is **conditional uniqueness** `[KND]`:

> **One operational alias must resolve unambiguously to one active target inside the consequence-bearing command domain, channel, scope and interval.**

The same alias may be reused in another scope, in another interval, or wherever no ambiguity can arise. **A high-consequence act whose target resolves only through an ambiguous alias is blocked** until explicitly disambiguated. A temporary disambiguating alias gets its own attributable, scoped, effective-dated binding; it **changes no stable identity, transfers no authority**, and must be referenced by subsequent evidence. **Implementation binds to Identity, Agent Runtime and Build OS. No alias system is minted here.**

### §E14.7.4 — Endpoint cessation, vacancy, transfer and succession

> **Cessation changes relations; it does not replace identity or rewrite history** `[KND]`.

**Five non-collapses** `[KND]`: `cessation ≠ deletion` · `succession ≠ sameness` · `replacement ≠ transfer` · `transfer ≠ inheritance of all relations` · `vacancy ≠ implied authority`.

A `RelationTypeDefinition` **declares or references** enough cessation/succession semantics to determine: historical survival after endpoint cessation · termination of current force · residual obligations · transferability / delegability / non-transferability · whether a **new** assertion, decision, grant or admission is required · revalidation on owner, holder or endpoint change · vacancy/orphan posture · rightful succession authority. **No universal survival enum is frozen** `[CAN→4]`.

**A successor** has a distinct identity, is related to its predecessor through **explicit lineage**, and receives **only** expressly transferred or newly conferred rights, authority, obligations, custody or work. It does not acquire prior authorship, does not rewrite prior acts, does not inherit non-transferable grants, and **does not become the predecessor** `[KND]`.

**Consequences, stated because each is a live failure shape** `[KND]`: a departed actor does not make work disappear · a departed holder does not make the seat disappear · a ceased principal does not make OMNI the owner · a missing successor remains **vacancy / unresolved authority** and blocks wherever the decision condition requires a current eligible holder (`§4.5`, and `§E13.8`'s holder-resolution axis).

**Revalidation on material change is candidate synthesis, corroborated by class-D evidence** `[KND]` — wave-6 `285`: *"review once, inherit many — but re-review every material departure from the certified envelope."* **The corpus signal confers no force; it establishes that the rule was already routed.**

## §E14.8 — Rejection-ground matrix and fixtures

### §E14.8.1 — The matrix

**This is the deliverable `§G1-CONTRACT` row 3 asks for.** Each ground names what is rejected, on what basis, and with what consequence. **Rejection is decidable and attributable; it is not the same as well-formedness.** **This table is the authoritative row set — no count of it is maintained anywhere else in the carrier.**

**"Reject" is not one consequence, and a validator that emits only `reject` is unusable** `[KND]`. The semantic classes below must stay distinguishable; **no final universal consequence enum is settled here** `[CAN→6]`:

| Consequence class | Meaning | Remedy shape |
|---|---|---|
| **malformed** | the assertion violates its type contract | fix the assertion |
| **unauthorized** | the actor lacked authority to assert, admit or constrain | obtain authority — resolution is `§G1-AUTH`'s |
| **unadmitted** | valid at origin, not effective here — **semantics or instance** | admit, map, or leave excluded; **never deleted** |
| **nonconforming** | violates a cardinality, exclusivity or non-loosening requirement | change the assertion or the declared constraint |
| **stale** | pinned constituents have advanced past what the query requires | regenerate or re-admit |
| **unresolved / partial** | coverage or authority set incomplete | report `unknown`/`partial`, **never clean** |
| **temporarily blocked** | an interim measure or unresolved conflict suspends use | resolve the conflict or let the measure lapse |
| **unanswerable** | the model cannot answer the question asked of it | narrow the question — do not answer confidently |
| **repairable locator failure** | identity intact, pointer broken | repair the pointer, **not the identity** |

| # | Ground | Rejected object | Basis | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | undeclared or invalid endpoint type | assertion | `§E14.2` type contract | reject — malformed |
| R2 | unknown endpoint identity | assertion | resolvability class 3 | reject |
| R3 | broken locator, identity intact | **the locator, not the assertion** | class 2 | repair pointer; flag projection |
| R4 | no governing `RelationTypeDefinition` revision pinned | assertion | `§E14.3` | reject |
| R5 | issuer lacks authority to assert this type in this scope | assertion | `§E14.2` authority requirements | reject |
| R6 | cardinality violated **at its declared binding site** | assertion / admission / projection | `§E14.4.2` | reject at that site only |
| R7 | declared exclusivity violated | the co-occurring set | `§E14.4.3` | reject or fail closed per consequence |
| R8 | `specializes` relaxes an inherited prohibition | the specializing definition | `§E14.4.4` | reject |
| R9 | composition asserted with **no declared rule** for the pair | path result | `§E14.4.5` | reject — no valid composition |
| R10 | derived result presented as a direct assertion | path result | non-collapse 3 | reject |
| R11 | authority, ownership or approval right claimed **from reachability** | the claim | authority non-propagation | reject |
| R12 | inherited upstream edge added **without recorded classification** | the new edge | `D0CKPT-GRD-005` | reject — and **this is not detectable by well-formedness** |
| R13 | edge inferred from grouping, ordering or co-membership | the edge | `D0CKPT-DEC-009` | reject |
| R14 | direction inverted — supplier read as dependent | the edge | `D0CKPT-GRD-005` | reject |
| R15 | a would-be superseder **not carrying binding normative effect** supersedes a predecessor that does | supersession transaction | `§E14.5` | reject |
| R16 | supersession by rank comparison | supersession transaction | no ordering anywhere | reject |
| R17 | projection whose input manifest omits temporal mode or a bound | projection | `§E14.5` | reject — not reproducible |
| R18 | as-of reconstruction using facts not knowable at the cutoff, in a no-hindsight mode | projection | `§E14.5` | reject |
| R19 | projection consumed while its pinned constituents have advanced | projection | invalidation predicate | reject as stale |
| R20 | clean closure reported over partial coverage | traversal result | `§E13.8` | reject the **posture**, not the result |
| R21 | non-waivable requirement dropped because no edge was drawn | approval condition | `G1-FIND-50` | reject — requirement is policy-resolved |
| R22 | typed absence read as denial | resolution | `§E14.3` | reject |
| R23 | foreign assertion treated as locally binding without admission | effective edge | `G1-FIND-46` | exclude, never delete |
| R24 | admission that mutates the origin assertion | admission decision | object 3 | reject |
| R25 | conflict recorded as a state value on an edge | conflict handling | object 5 | reject |
| R26 | silent winner where policy requires review | resolution | `§E14.6` | fail closed, named owner + reason |
| R27 | deletion of a losing or non-effective assertion | the deletion | preservation rules | reject |
| R28 | `derived_from` inferred from similarity or behavioural equivalence | lineage claim | `§E14.7.2` | reject |
| R29 | identity match used to create a relationship | the edge | Federation: never auto-share on identity match | reject |
| R30 | high-consequence act whose target resolves only via an ambiguous alias | the act | `§E14.7.3` | block until disambiguated |
| R31 | successor treated as the predecessor, or inheriting non-transferable grants | succession claim | `§E14.7.4` | reject |
| R32 | active relation surviving endpoint cessation without required revalidation | the relation's current force | `§E14.7.4` | terminate current force; preserve history |
| R33 | vacancy resolved by silent steward or operator fallback | authority resolution | `vacancy ≠ implied authority` | reject; block per decision condition |
| R34 | ownership edge from a P4/P5 resource to canonical truth | the edge | `T0-15`, `D0THES-DEC-033` | reject — while **`owns_definition` remains permitted, read as the exact scoped semantic-authority / definition-ownership fact over a definition resource** (`§E9.3`), **never as generic `owns` returning through a side door** (`R42`) |
| R35 | historically consequential object **lacks the temporal fields** the requested mode requires | the **query**, not the object | `§E14.5` matrix | fail — *unanswerable*, never a confident answer |
| R36 | foreign assertion whose governing **predicate semantics fail `predicate_semantics_usable`** for the receiving scope and declared temporal query — no base usability, no usable one-hop mapping, no authorized mapping path | effective edge | `§E14.3.2`–`§E14.3.4` | exclude as **unadmitted semantics** — **distinct from `R23`**, which is instance-level usability |
| R37 | a **mapping treated as identity or equality** | the mapping claim | `§E14.3.1` rule 4 | reject |
| R38 | a **stale or superseded mapping** used without required revalidation | effective edge | `§E14.3.1` rule 5 · `§E14.2.1` | exclude as stale |
| R39 | an object's **structural field reified as an assertion** to bypass its authority, lifecycle or validation | the assertion | `§E14.1.3` | reject |
| R40 | `conflicts_with` **substituted for a governed `ConflictRecord`** | the conflict handling | `§E14.1.3` consequence 2 | reject — detection is not adjudication |
| R41 | cross-owner **constraint** declared without a resolved affected-authority set | the constraint | `§E14.4.1` | block — never default to a steward |
| R42 | **`owns`** asserted as a relation type | the edge | `§E14.2.2` | reject — resolve to the exact governance relation |
| R43 | **provenance that cannot be verified** presented as an established graph fact | the claim's **force**, not the record | authority basis required (`§E14.2`) | admit as a **recorded claim with unverified provenance**; fail closed wherever consequence requires verified authority |
| R44 | mapping assertion whose **governing type does not declare mapping semantics** | the assertion | `§E14.3.3` discriminant | **malformed** — it is not a mapping |
| R45 | mapping's **governing mapping type is not `type_base_usable`** in the receiving scope | the mapping's participation | `§E14.3.3` · guard ④ | **unadmitted semantics** — the mapping type is itself foreign and unadmitted |
| R46 | mapping's **target type is not `type_base_usable`** | the mapping's participation | `§E14.3.3` | **unusable translation target** — and specifically **not** repairable by another mapping |
| R47 | mapping used to **confer applicability without sufficient applicability authority or an active mapping admission** | the applicability effect, not the record | `§E14.3.4` | **unauthorized applicability act** — the mapping survives as candidate, evidence or proposal |
| R48 | **mapping chain used with no applicable `CompositionRule`** | the derived path | `§E14.3.3` | **invalid composition** — default-deny, never silently allowed |
| R49 | **cyclic or unbounded mapping path** | the evaluation | `§E14.3.3` cycle-safety | **unanswerable or invalid composition** — never silently resolved to usable |
| R50 | **foreign type treated as local** by name, content, copied carrier or catalog placement | the ownership claim | `§E14.3.2` `own_effective_type` · `§E12.7.1` | **identity / admission bypass** — a fork is a new identity, and the foreign assertion still needs a mapping plus its assertion decision |

**Mapped result presented as a direct assertion** is **`R10`**, which covers derived-as-direct generally and **explicitly includes the mapping case** (`§E14.3.3` lineage law). **It is not duplicated here** — one ground, one row.

**The decisive property:** **R12, R13, R14, R20, R21 and R30 are invisible to well-formedness checking.** A validator that type-checks endpoints and cardinalities passes every one of them. That is why the acceptance condition is a property of the *model*, not of a schema.

## §E15.0 — Assignment, force classification and the founding statement

**The assignment, from live state.** `§G1-CONTRACT` row 4 names the sources `§E1 AB-07` + `§6.4`, the decision state `INCOMPLETE`, the residual *"field additions and release postures, not a state model,"* and the acceptance condition *"full state model incl. the five change classes."* `§G1-CONTRACT.c` row 4 requires *"what happens when the source, contract, operator policy, product classification, or the applicability decision itself changes."* R9 `§6.4` states the diagnosis this output exists to answer: the estate has fragments — Build Entry, AWP `§5`, the supersession ledger, the catalog — and **nothing states how a proposed architecture change is raised, evaluated, accepted, rejected or superseded, nor who may.** Plan root requirement **3 · EVOLVABLE** supplies the nine required verbs; G4 **test 10** supplies the proof shape.

**The founding statement has two halves at two different force levels. Bundling them is how a candidate construction acquires constitutional standing it was never granted** (`G1-FIND-73`, `G1-FIND-85`).

> **① INHERITED CONSTITUTIONAL POSITION** `[INH]` — **there is no single architecture-change state machine, no single terminal state, no single writer and no single owner of historical truth.** Accepted Output 2 models an architecture change as **one correlated operation decomposed into owner-scoped commitments, deterministic derivations, attributed observations, durable obligations and continuous controllers** — explicitly *not* a globally atomic transaction and *never one writable lifecycle scalar* (`§E13.2`, `§E13.10`). Accepted Output 3 forbids stamping one field set across objects with different physics (`§E14.5`). `D0THES-GRD-035` forbids one domain owning a cross-cutting concern. `D0CKPT-GRD-003` forbids duplicated state.

> **② CANDIDATE OUTPUT-4 CONSTRUCTION** `[KND]` — **that position is realized as a register of lifecycle-bearing subjects, each with its own typed lifecycle contract owned by the subject's rightful owner, joined by a minimal shared reference algebra; a change's *character* is a set of **independently owned, scope- and time-qualified characterization records** composed into profiles under named policies, rather than an exactly-one class; and a change's *progress* is a derived projection over separately owned facts rather than a stored status.**

**Four provenance classes, at four different force levels** (`GRD-036`, `G1-FIND-40`, `F-11`):

**The authority composition Output 4 references and does not own** `[INH]`. **One composed authority model, not two competing ones.** `rbac_authority_contract.md §5` defines the **four top-level admissibility functions** a consequential action must satisfy — Federation admits cross-boundary possibility · RBAC decides actor capability, **including consent gating** · the owning domain commits · CNS-Meta enforces and audits. `D0THES-DEC-035` names the **six authoritative fact owners that composition requires** — Identity, Federation, RBAC, D7, CNS-Meta and the owning domain. **Identity and D7 are independently owned inputs to the composition: a missing or invalid identity, represented principal or consent record blocks action through the applicable function.** `capability_envelope` (what a model or tool may do) and `delegated_authority_envelope` (what an actor may do for a principal, under scope, purpose, TTL and revocation) are **distinct primitives**, and non-human delegated authority is decomposed across Identity + RBAC + Federation + D7 — never owned by the AI registry.

**Output 4 defines, owns and amends none of it.** What it takes from the model is exactly three constraints: every effect-producing transition **references** an authority basis resolved through that composition (`§E15.2`) · **`GRD-031` — Federation does not absorb Identity, RBAC capability, the consent record, AI capability envelopes, domain commits or CNS-Meta enforcement**, which is why `§E15.4.5` does not make generic scope Federation's · **`DEC-036` — cross-boundary emit and ingest run through one governed spine**, which is why `§E15.6` and `§E15.9` reference it rather than build a second. **`GRD-029`** — CNS orchestrates and owns no truth — is consonant with every projection law already stated here.

**One classification the split makes necessary, because this output leans on class D harder than any predecessor did.** The Platform, Care and Accountability captures contain the estate's only existing per-object release/deployment/rollout/migration lifecycles, its only exposure-depth ladder, and its sharpest statements of `rollback ≠ recall` and *system fix ≠ individual remedy*. **All of it is `analysis_nonbinding` and none of it is closed.** It is cited below as **corroboration that defeats this output's novelty claims**, and every law it corroborates is stated over a class-A or class-B carrier or marked as candidate Output-4 synthesis. `G1-FIND-87`, `G1-FIND-91`.

## §E15.1 — The lifecycle-bearing subject register

**The center of Output 4. This is a distinguishability and fact-ownership requirement, not an ownership claim** `[KND]`. Output 4 does not reauthor these subjects; it names which source owns each, and defines how its own contracts compose with them.

**The splitting rule, which governs the register and replaces any count** `[KND]`. **Two subjects are separate whenever any of these differ: logical identity · authoritative owner · transition authority · clocks · admissible transitions · failure physics · termination or survival behaviour · conformance consequence.** Rows are keyed, not numbered, and **no total is stated anywhere** (`F-06`) — a maintained subject count is a derived value that drifts the moment the register grows, and it carries no architectural information. *A row bearing two owners or two clocks is a fusion wearing a slash.*

**Completeness posture, because removing the count must not remove the closure claim** `[INH §E13.8]`. This register is a **declared-open minimum, not a census.** Coverage expansion is measurable and reported, and claiming the register is complete would be the population-versus-sample defect `G1-FIND-74` records.

**But "not represented here" and "no facts yet" are different failures and must not share the token `unknown`** `[KND]` — see `§E15.4.4` for the full coverage algebra. In summary: **a modeled subject with missing facts is evidence-unknown** and may enter bootstrap or degraded operation under a named authority and the inherited non-derogable floor. **An affected subject kind that is not in the model at all is a classification gap**, and it cannot be governed that way — you cannot record residual risk against clocks, authority, consequence or survival rules you have not identified, because you do not know what you are risking. It **fails closed for the affected consequence and scope**, and where it is discovered after approval it **invalidates the assessment basis that approval pinned** rather than reporting an unknown. **A third state exists and must be attributed, not assumed: authoritatively established out-of-scope**, which is an attributed decision that the subject kind does not apply here.

> **An unresolved owner is recorded as unresolved, and it blocks EXACTLY the transitions that require it** `[KND]`. Where a transition's decision condition requires the target authority and none resolves, **`owner_set_complete` is false for that transition** and it fails closed `[INH §E13.10`, `§E13.8]`. **It is not false globally.** Accepted `owner_set_complete` is scoped to *"every authority **required for the consequence class**"* — so an unresolved environment authority blocks environment-authority-requiring transitions and leaves every other transition alone. *Reading it globally would make the open `environment` question halt the entire deployment plane until the estate settles a matter Output 4 is forbidden to settle.* **Output 4 does not resolve environment ownership; it refuses to paper over it.**

> **The register's law** `[KND]`: **each row's canonical fact has exactly one authoritative owner in scope** `[INH §E13.7]`, **each row declares its own admissible transitions and clocks**, and **no row's lifecycle value is readable as another row's.** Publication says nothing about admission; admission says nothing about adoption; adoption says nothing about deployment; deployment says nothing about activation; activation says nothing about effective use; none of them says anything about conformance; and a conformance claim says nothing about whether conformance currently holds. **Most rows are owned outside Output 4** — the ownership column is the enumeration, and no tally of it is maintained here.

> **Compatibility impact is dimension-qualified, and the dimensions are REFERENCED rather than restated** `[KND]`. The direction above is scoped to **one** dimension — the **admissible instance set** — and **a single direction cannot represent compatibility impact**, because the dimensions move independently and sometimes oppositely. *Adding a required field narrows the admissible instance set while widening the behavioural obligation on producers; widening an enum invalidates no existing instance while breaking consumers that exhaustively matched, or otherwise assumed closure over, the prior value set.* **A change can therefore narrow on one dimension, widen on another, and be `incomparable` on a third — which is why a single scalar hides exactly the disagreement that has to stay visible** (the same law `§E15.6` states for the frontier and `§E15.4.4` for coverage).
>
> **The other dimensions are separate facts with their own owners, and this row duplicates none of them** `[KND]`: **semantic meaning** is already `semantic_compatibility_assessments[]`, an independently owned record family at `§E15.4.2` carrying accepted Output-3 axis ① `[INH §E14.2.1]` · **behavioural requirements**, **defaults and precedence** and **consumer compatibility** are the affected subject owner's and, where a consumer relied on an emitted contract, are evidenced through `§E15.4.2`'s reliance observations and `§E15.6`'s frontier records · **migration impact** is `required_treatment_determinations[]` and `§E15.8` · **conformance and non-loosening judgment is OUTPUT 6's** and is stated here in no form (`G1-FIND-23`). **Restating any of them as fields inside this row would be `D0CKPT-GRD-003` committed inside its own repair** — two predicates built at G2 from one fact, arriving through vocabulary. **Reference the owning result; add no mandatory field set** (`G1-FIND-106`).

## §E15.2 — The minimal lifecycle algebra, and what it may never impose

**A shared reference layer exists so the subject contracts can be joined, compared and reconstructed. It is a reference algebra, not a record shape, and it imposes no schema** `[KND]`. **Record *families* are not tables**: how any of this is physicalized, indexed or stored is G2's, and a reader who turns a family into a table has made an implementation choice this output does not make.

**Every lifecycle-bearing transition, in every contract, resolves the following** — as a **semantic requirement**, not a mandatory column set:

| Element | Requirement |
|---|---|
| subject identity + subject type | which register row, which instance, which revision |
| scope | the exact scope the transition binds — operator · deployment · jurisdiction · profile · target · cohort · namespace. **A transition with no declared scope is not evaluable** |
| authoritative owner or issuer | who owns the fact this transition creates |
| **authority-basis reference** | a pointer to the law, contract, right, policy, role, prior commitment or attributed decision the transition rests on. **A reference, never an authority definition** (`§E15.0`; `§G1-AUTH` owns the ontology). Where the actor is non-human, the basis may cite an externally owned **`delegated_authority_envelope`** — **which Output 4 neither defines nor owns** `[INH DEC-035]`. Three inherited constraints hold: **actor identity, represented principal, capability and commit authority remain distinct** · **no actor inherits the identity of the principal that invoked it** — impersonation is the named anti-pattern, not a shortcut · and **authority is revalidated at the point of consequence**, which is `acceptance_currently_usable`, not a one-time check `[INH §E13.10]` |
| temporal interpretation | which clocks this transition carries, per the object's own physics `[INH §E14.5]` |
| transition / effect identity | the transition's own identity, and where an effect is emitted, the **effect-scoped** idempotency key `[INH §E13.4]` |
| causal + correlation references | parent, cause, correlation to the operation, and the **existing** architecture-semantic event vocabulary `[INH §E13.5]` — **Output 4 mints no second event engine** |
| supersession · migration · compensation · correction links | typed relations to prior and successor acts |
| evidence + uncertainty posture | what is known, what is unknown, what is unreachable, and what is merely claimed |

**What the algebra may never impose** `[KND]` — each prohibition inherits a named accepted or governing source:

- **one universal state enum** — `§E13.10`: the predicates are derived over separately owned facts and are *never one writable lifecycle scalar*;
- **one universal terminal state** — `§E13.18`: at fleet scale there is no single moment when the architecture is uniformly deployed; corroborated by the class-D **four-horizons** finding that technical repair, clinical reassessment, party remedy and recurrence monitoring **close independently but linked**;
- **one universal bitemporal storage shape** — `§E14.5`: temporal semantics are stated *by object physics*, and stamping one field set across objects with different physics is the `F-08` failure Output 1 spent four passes removing;
- **one universal writer** — `§E13.7` one-authoritative-owner-per-fact-in-scope, and `D0THES-GRD-035`;
- **one global event owner or history owner** — `§E15.11`;
- **one global transition authority** — `§G1-AUTH`, and the canonical 4-way composition in which *none replaces the others*.

> **This shape is inherited, not invented** `[INH]`. **`C4.4 §R`'s 13-question mechanism template already requires every mechanism to declare its own (6) authority/admission/commit boundary, (7) lifecycle states + closure, (8) partial-failure/degraded/unknown/quarantine/retry posture, and (9) temporal/as-of/correction/supersession/deletion/revocation semantics.** Output 4's per-subject contract is that template applied to the change plane. `G1-FIND-88` records the consequence: **`AB-01`/`B-13` is separately generalizing the same template as a G1 obligation, and no surface coordinates the two.**

## §E15.3 — The change-operation lifecycle, and why `state` is a projection

**Accepted Output 2 routes "the Change Manifest lifecycle enum" to Output 4 and simultaneously constrains it: `Output 2 owns the predicates and which object owns each fact — they are derived over separately owned facts and are never one writable lifecycle scalar`** `[INH §E13.10]`.

**Therefore the proposal is a set of independently evaluable lifecycle predicates with a named source each, and not a stored status** `[KND]`.

> **Inherited predicate names are used exactly, and no parallel name is minted** `[KND]`. Where a condition already has an accepted Output-2 name, that name appears here unchanged. **A synonym in a successor output is how two predicates get built at G2 from one fact** — `D0CKPT-GRD-003`, arriving through vocabulary rather than through storage.
>
> **These are milestones, not phases, and the distinction is load-bearing** `[KND]`. **They coexist.** `accepted_historically` is permanent while `acceptance_currently_usable` can turn false beside it; `landed` can hold while `effective(...)` does not; several can be true, stale and false simultaneously across different scopes. **The projection is a set or structured view of concurrently evaluable predicates, never a single selected value** — calling them phases is precisely the invitation a UI, schema or vendor adapter needs to collapse them back into one enum, which is the failure this section exists to prevent. **Any materialized view of them is read-only, generation-stamped, invalidatable, and prohibited as an input authority unless re-derived from its owning facts** `[INH §E13.9]`.

**Before any of it: the admission contract, which decides whether this lifecycle has a subject at all** `[CAN]`. **This output defined a lifecycle for changes without ever saying what makes something a change** — the defect `G1-FIND-105` records. **R2.6 states the contract and withdraws the overbroad form an earlier pass gave it.**

> **What Output 4 owns here, and what it must never own** `[KND]`. **Output 4 owns the ADMISSION CONTRACT** — the typed classification result this lifecycle will accept, the fail-closed default, and the blocking behaviour on an unresolved result. **It owns nothing about who classifies, under what authority, or by what method.** *Both collapses of that distinction are failures, and they run in opposite directions.* **Collapsing toward *"Output 4 classifies everything"*** makes this output the universal owner of configuration, drift, nonconformance, exception, emergency activity, domain operation and conformance classification — the cross-cutting god-object `D0THES-GRD-035` forbids, and the shape an earlier form of this section committed. **Collapsing toward *"Output 4 owns no admission"*** leaves the entry seam ungoverned, and **at machine change volume that means every surface reinvents a classifier and the substrate loses the one seam it exists to hold** — which is the current-practice failure `§E15.17.6 B` records for this very capability. **Stated so the second half cannot be misread as "the classification is unowned"** `[KND]`: **Output 4 owns the admission contract. Every classification result is attributable to the rightful determining authority or an authorized generator, under a named authority or policy basis. Output 4 consumes that result and enforces its admission, routing or blocking consequence. Output 4 does not own the classifier, its authority, or its method.** **Routed is not ownerless** — the same law `§E14.1.2` states for generated results and `§E15.1` states for every register row.

> **What makes the classification result *typed*, bound by reference so it cannot degrade into a boolean at G2** `[CAN]`. A "typed classification result" that stays an English promise is an invitation for every surface to ship its own flag. **It inherits the attribution and temporal discipline accepted Output 3 already proved for local admission** (`§E14.3`/`§E14.3.1`: issued by the rightful scope over an exact revision-pinned target of a declared class, carrying its own outcome, conditions, disposition and effective interval). **Applied here, a classification result resolves:** the **exact subject or revision and scope** · the **attributed outcome** · the **determining authority or authorized generator** · the **authority or policy basis** · the **decision condition** where one is required · **conditions** · **recorded time, and an effective interval where the result carries normative force** · and an **evidence or method reference where the result is derived rather than attributed.** **This is a reference to a proven envelope, not a new object** — Output 4 does **not** assert that its classification result is the same object as an `AdmissionDecision`, and physicalization remains G2's.

**The scope guard comes first, because without it every act in the estate becomes an architecture change** `[KND]`. This law applies **only to architecture-owned subjects, or to subjects whose architecture relevance has been established.** Everything else resolves through `§E15.1`'s third state — **authoritatively established out-of-scope, which is an attributed decision and never an assumption.** *A clinical order deviates from no architecture, and the absence of a variation point says nothing whatever about it.*

**The source of the test, at its true force** `[CAN]`. Charter R9 `§6.2` carries the SEI product-line mechanism verbatim: *"the architecture declares, in advance, where deviation is permitted and how. Anything inside a declared variation point is **configuration**. Anything outside it is a **change to the architecture**, which goes through the architecture's own change process — not a customer's ticket."* **R9 is `analysis_nonbinding`, and its own passport reads *"Binds nothing. Promotes nothing. Mints no name, category or artifact class."*** It is therefore a **G0-chartered candidate mechanism G1 must reconcile and validate**, and an assignment input — **evidence, not installed law.** This carrier already withdrew the *"accepted answer"* reading of this exact charter section (`§7.3`), and *an R2.5 form of `G1-FIND-105` called it "governing force"; that is withdrawn here.*

**The admission outcomes, routed to homes that already exist** `[CAN]`. **This is a routing law, not a taxonomy.** Almost every outcome below already has an owner inside `§E15` or outside it, and the contract's job is to point at it — **no new closed enum, no new object family, no fourteenth subject-register row.** **The list is non-exhaustive by construction**, and a result matching none of these rows resolves to row 7 rather than to a default.

| # | Admission outcome | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **declared and authorized variation / configuration** — the subject sits inside a current, applicable variation point and within its authority envelope. **Two distinct acts live here and the SEI primary separates them** — see below | governed by **that variation point's own bounds and authority.** Not ungoverned, and **not this lifecycle's subject** |
| 2 | **proposed architecture change** — a proposal to alter architecture-owned semantics, structure, requirements or permitted variation | **admitted to this lifecycle**; may satisfy `intake_recorded` |
| 3 | **observed implementation drift or nonconformance** | `§E15.4.1`'s **divergence → finding-candidate → evidence → admission** chain, and `§E15.8` law 1's drift-versus-envelope test. **An observed condition is not a submitted manifest revision and is never forced through `intake_recorded`** |
| 4 | **unauthorized local configuration** — an act that already occurred with no resolvable basis | `§E15.7`'s posture axis and the `§E15.4.1` chain. **An already-occurred unauthorized act is never silently converted into a proposed change**: the two have different owners, different clocks and different remedies |
| 5 | **domain operation outside architecture-change scope** | `§E15.1`'s **authoritatively established out-of-scope** — an attributed decision by the authority that owns the scope question |
| 6 | **authorized exception, waiver, emergency activity or accepted risk** | its **own externally owned authority and regime.** The emergency and degraded-mode regime stays routed to **`AB-29` / G3** (`§E15.17.1`), and `§E15.8` already carries accepted risk as a residual-risk statement inside an envelope. **Not automatically an ordinary change proposal** |
| 7 | **undetermined classification, or a model gap** | **typed absence** `[INH §E12.7]`, recorded as a **classification gap.** It **BLOCKS lifecycle characterization** (`§E15.4.4`) until a rightful classifier resolves it, and it is **not bootstrappable** (`§E15.1`) |

> **Row 1 is two acts, not one — read from the SEI primary, with the citations corrected at R2.6.2** `[CAN]`. `CMU/SEI-2005-TR-012` (Bachmann & Clements, *Variability in Software Product Lines*, CMU/SEI 2005), **Appendix, explaining Figure 6** — *not* `§3`, which is *"The Goal of Variability"*: *"**In many cases, a variable part will include at least two mechanisms: one to support the creation of new variants (New Variant Mechanism) and another to support the selection of existing variants (Selection Mechanism).**"* **Selecting an existing variant and creating a new one are different mechanisms**, and nothing obliges them to carry the same authority. The discriminator is **Bosch's open/closed distinction, which the report adopts at `§2.2`** (*"Selection and Modification vs. Creation"*): *"**'open' variability (with room for new variants)**"* versus *"**'closed' variability (in which the number of variants is fixed)."*
>
> **What the primary says, and where OMNI's inference begins — kept apart** `[KND]`. **The primary's New Variant Mechanism operates INSIDE a declared variable part**: it is the pre-authorized way a product developer produces a variant the core-asset developer planned for — the report's own example is a supplied template for writing a product-specific chapter, with the Selection Mechanism then inserting it. **So creating a variant through an open variable part's own New Variant Mechanism is configuration in SEI's terms, and this output treats it as row 1.** **The mapping of the *closed* case to row 2 is OMNI inference, not an SEI statement:** the report says a closed variable part has a fixed variant count; it does not say that adding one is *"a change to the architecture."* **OMNI draws that consequence** because a variant appearing where no mechanism authorizes one is a deviation with no resolvable basis. **Also kept apart:** `§2.2`'s *"Creation"* category — generators whose output *"resembles neither the generator nor the input"* — is a **different distinction** about how product assets derive from core assets, and it is **not** the Appendix's create-versus-select split. *An R2.6.1 form of this note ran the two together and mis-addressed all three passages.*
>
> **So:** selection within a current variation point is row 1. **Creating a new variant is row 1 where the point is declared OPEN and the actor holds that point's new-variant authority; where the point is closed, or that authority does not resolve, this output treats the creation as row 2.** *Neither R2.5 nor R2.6 carried the split at all: both treated "inside a variation point" as a single outcome, which would have let a new variant appear inside a closed point as ordinary configuration.* **Whether a variation point is open or closed, and who holds its new-variant authority, are properties of the variation point — externally owned, not minted here.** **And no product-line ownership assumption transfers:** SEI's core-asset-developer ⟂ product-developer division is a software-product-line organizational form, and OMNI's authority composition is `§G1-AUTH`'s (`GRD-033`).
>
> **One operational precedent for the same separation, from a different domain** `[class D]`. **OpenRewrite's `ScanningRecipe` runs three declared phases** (read at R2.6.2): *"**1.** A scanning phase that collects information while making **no new code changes**… **2.** An optional **generating** phase where new files are created… **3.** An **editing** phase where the recipe makes changes,"* with all scanning visitors seeing *"the state before any changes are made by any recipe edit visitor,"* and recipes held **immutable** for the same input and configuration. **That is assessment ⟂ generation ⟂ mutation as three separately ordered acts** — the same shape `§E15.4.1` states when it makes an assessment *"a required input to approval, NOT the approval artifact."* **Corroboration only, conferring no force.** **The adapter obligation it implies is ROUTED, not stated here** `[CAN→7 · G2]`: *a transformation adapter must expose its scan and applicability evidence separately from its generation and its mutation, and declare its own idempotency boundary* — **that is a per-mechanism transfer constraint, which is Output 7's, and an adapter contract, which is G2's.** *Output 4 owns the generic separation and must not carry a tooling requirement inside its structural acceptance core; an R2.6.2 form of this note stated the adapter obligation as Output-4 law.* No OpenRewrite object is imported.

> **`Absence is not permission` survives; `absence establishes architecture-change identity` does not** `[KND]`. Where no variation point covers a deviation, the answer is **not** `configuration` — that reading is exactly how a thousand operator tweaks become invisible drift. **But it is not automatically row 2 either.** **Absence routes to governed classification and may block use or progression**, which is the fail-closed direction that keeps both errors off the table at once: nothing is waved through, and nothing acquires architecture-change identity by default. *An R2.5 form of this section made absence establish row 2 outright, which silently made this output the owner of drift, emergency activity and every out-of-scope domain act.*

> **Two consequences for values this output had already inherited** `[KND]`. **①** `§E15.4.4`'s coverage law needs a denominator, and it is **row 2** — the population **admitted as architecture-change candidates.** Rows 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are not in it, and row 7 is neither and blocks. Without that, coverage was a ratio over an undefined population. **②** `authorized_variation`, inherited unchanged in Output 2's seven-value posture baseline `[INH §E13.18]`, asserts a difference is **authorized** and named no authorizing object. **It now references one — and the basis type is an OPEN set, of which a variation point is one member** (`§E15.7`). *An R2.5 form of this section asserted that `authorized_variation` **is** the SEI variation-point mechanism under another name. **That equivalence is withdrawn*** — see `§E15.7` and `G1-FIND-105`.

> **What is deliberately not minted here** `[KND]`: the **structure** of a variation point — its facets, binding time, admissible bounds, and how overlapping points resolve — is **not** authored by this output. `binding_time` is `[CAN→3/5]` per `§E8.6`'s relabelling of `G1-FIND-24`, resolution across points is **Output 5**'s, and the installed form is **G2**'s. **Output 4 states the admission contract and references the variation point as an externally owned basis** — one reference, not a new object.
>
> **On the name — and a claim R2.6.1 got wrong about its own estate, retracted here** `[KND]`. `CMU/SEI-2005-TR-012` **`§2.4`** declines *variation point* in favour of **`variable part`** for two reasons: the container reason, and *"**Second, variation point is often used to describe variations in terms that refer to an asset's externally visible properties or functions rather than places in the asset's internal structure.**"* The second reason is the material one — **OMNI's subject IS the externally visible property, what an operator may deviate on, not a location in internal source structure** — so the report's own wording places OMNI's usage on the side the term customarily names.
>
> ***R2.6.1 claimed the estate "never captured" that second reason. That is false and is retracted.*** **Output 1 `§E7.1.6` already quotes both reasons in full**; `§E8.6` then narrowed only the *"SEI declines the term"* framing to *"the 2005 report declines it; other SEI work uses it; do not generalize."* **So this is vocabulary corroboration of a standing Output-1 decision, not a new finding** — and the decision itself is unchanged: **OMNI keeps `variation point`** (charter `§6.2`; Build OS `09`'s vocabulary-discipline clause forbids minting a synonym). *The mechanism of the error is worth more than the error: R2.6.1 asserted novelty against the estate **without grepping the estate** — `L-5`'s claim-outliving-its-source, committed inside a pass whose whole purpose was source fidelity.* *(Separately: an R2.5 pass minted `variation declaration` as a parallel name in this section, four paragraphs after the no-synonym law it states. Withdrawn at R2.6.)*

| Lifecycle predicate / milestone `[CAN]` | Derived from | Owner of the underlying fact |
|---|---|---|
| `intake_recorded` | a submission event exists for a manifest revision **whose subject was admitted as a proposed architecture change — row 2 of the admission contract above.** An observed condition (rows 3 and 4) has no manifest revision and no submitter, and is **never forced through this milestone** | Architecture Operations |
| `impact_claimed` | `impact_current` holds over the exact manifest revision, base, graph, ruleset and coverage posture | the derivation's generator contract |
| `owner_set_complete` | every owner and non-waivable authority **required for the consequence class** has resolved `[INH §E13.10 — inherited name, no alias minted]` | the authority resolver |
| `decided` | `decision_condition_satisfied` **and** no blocking refusal, stay, expired condition or invalid grant remains | each deciding authority, separately |
| `accepted_historically` | an authority-bearing acceptance referencing the exact revision set — **a permanent historical fact** | the accepting authority |
| `acceptance_currently_usable` | that acceptance is still usable for a landing or effect **now** `[INH §E13.10 — inherited name, no alias minted]` | derived over grants, policy, conformance basis |
| `landed` | an integration receipt proves the exact accepted set was applied to the named target | the integration holder |
| `effective(scope, …)` | origin validity ∧ local admission ∧ activation ∧ profile applicability ∧ interval ∧ non-revocation, **for that scope** | jointly origin and receiving scope `[INH §E13.18]` |

**Three laws follow** `[KND]`:

1. **`ChangeManifest.state`, if it exists at all, is an intake convenience, a derived projection, or a bounded workflow hint. It may never be the canonical truth from which acceptance, landing, effectiveness, conformance, reconciliation or authority is inferred.** A stored scalar duplicating these facts would be `D0CKPT-GRD-003` committed inside its own fix — the shape `G1-FIND-51` already forbade for staleness.
2. **The nine functions are a functional map, not an ordering guarantee** `[INH §E13.3]`. Propagation re-enters review; observation runs throughout; correction restarts the shape as a **new** operation with its own `correction_id`.
3. **Plan `§3.1`'s six-value list — `proposed / reviewed / approved / staged / landed / reverted` — is NOT adopted as canonical.** `§E15.4` records why, and `§E15.5` records what `reverted` actually is.

## §E15.4 — Change characterization: prospective assessment ⟂ observed consequence

**`C-03` is CLOSED as a requirement and this output does not reopen it: irreversible and forward-only change must be representable, and "evolvable" means *reversed where semantically safe — otherwise superseded, compensated, or advanced through explicit forward migration*.** What remains open is the vocabulary that happened to close it. Plan `§3.1` states *"every Change Manifest declares exactly one"* of five labels; `§G1-CONTRACT` row 4's acceptance condition names *"the five change classes"*; `§E13.23`, `§E14.9.4`, `§7.6` and `§7.7` each place the classes and the lifecycle enum in Output 4's scope and outside their own. **The labels are a governing obligation to disposition, not a ratified enum.**

**`G1-FIND-86` — the exactly-one field is not satisfiable, on the plan's own terms.** The five labels mix at least five independent facts, and the common healthcare cases satisfy two or three labels simultaneously: a forward-only public identifier that external consumers already rely on is **both** `forward_only` **and** `externally_committed`; a settled charge that can be credited but not un-charged is **both** `compensatable_not_reversible` **and** `externally_committed`; a schema change to an externally consumed contract is **both** `reversible_with_migration` **and** `externally_committed`. And the same `§3.1` cell places these five labels beside a state list terminating in `reverted`, **which three of the five forbid reaching.**

**And a second law the labels hide: a change's character is not one thing measured once.** Some of it is **assessed before the act** — is reversal semantically valid, what treatment will be required, what frontier do we expect to cross, what remedy would be available. Some of it is **observed after the act** — a frontier actually crossed, an effect emitted, reliance demonstrated, a clinical or financial consequence produced, a remedy executed. **A single characterization that mixes them mutates as the operation runs, which retroactively changes what an approval means.** That is the no-hindsight violation (`§E15.11`) committed against the approval record, and it is why `accepted_historically` ⟂ `acceptance_currently_usable` exists `[INH §E13.10]`.

### §E15.4.1 — Two characterizations, never one

| | **Prospective change assessments** | **Observed consequence projection** |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | **several independently attributable records**, each with its own identity and revision, per affected subject and scope (`§E15.4.2`) | a **derived projection** over execution and observation facts at a declared `as_of` |
| Who authors it | the **assessment issuer** for that fact and scope — a semantic authority, subject owner, accountable principal or domain owner, per family. **An issuer produces an attributed determination; it does not thereby decide anything** | **generated, and generated is not ownerless** `[INH §E14.1.2]`: a generator-contract owner · an authorized generator (identity + version) · a publication authority · an operational custodian · pinned inputs and lineage · an accountable verification path. **None of them owns the underlying facts** |
| What it is for | **a required input to approval — NOT the approval artifact.** The approval artifact is the **decision**, authored by the deciding authority. Plan `§3.1`'s *"a change may not be approved without a declared class"* is satisfied because the decision must reference an exact assessment basis, not because an assessment approves anything | answering *what has actually happened, as of when, at what coverage* |
| Temporal rule | **the decision references an exact, immutable assessment basis** (below). Later facts never mutate what was reviewed | resolved under `resolve(...)`, with mode and both bounds declared |
| What later facts may do | invalidate `acceptance_currently_usable` · change the observed projection · **cause obligations to be recognized from pre-existing bases** — never rewrite what was assessed and approved, and never originate a duty | — |

> **The assessment basis is a reference set, and its law is reference-only** `[CAN]`. A decision must be able to state **exactly what it reviewed**, and reconstructing that must not require trusting a mutable wrapper. The basis therefore pins: the exact **assessment-record revisions** · the **scope** they cover · the **aggregation-policy revision** used to compose them · the **coverage claim** · the temporal context · the governing policy or ruleset revisions.
>
> **Three constraints keep it from becoming the centralizer it exists to avoid** `[KND]`. **① It references and attests; it copies no substantive state** — the inherited `receipt` law `[INH §E13.4]`. The constituent judgments stay with their issuers. **② The basis must have a STABLE IDENTITY, so that "what this decision reviewed" is exactly reconstructable later.** Two realizations satisfy that and this output does not choose between them: the **immutable decision revision itself contains the exact reference set**, or the decision **cites an immutable reference-only receipt**. **③ No mandated wrapper document, and no mandated digest field.** A content digest over the reference set is a natural and likely encoding — and note it is a digest over *references*, not over judgments, since attributed judgments meet no determinism contract `[INH §E13.4]` — but **canonical serialization, hashing and storage are G2's**, and freezing them here would mint physicalization as architecture.
>
> **The failure this triad closes** `[KND]`: without stable identity, *"the exact basis"* is prose and an implementer supplies the missing object — which is the wrapper the first constraint forbids. **Stable identity plus reference-only is what makes the wrapper unnecessary rather than merely prohibited.** A decision that cannot stably identify and exactly reconstruct its assessment basis fails `CL-44`.

> **Divergence is a first-class derived condition, and it is scoped** `[CAN]`. Where the observed projection departs materially from the assessment basis a decision pinned — a change approved as reversible that crossed an external frontier, a remedy assessed as available that proved impossible — that divergence is a **detectable condition per affected scope**, not a global alarm: a change that diverged for three operators and not for twelve thousand has diverged in three scopes.
>
> **Detection does not open a finding** `[INH G1-FIND-60]`. The sequence is **divergence detected → finding candidate emitted → evidence and source recorded → admission decision → admitted finding, where authorized → obligations recognized from pre-existing bases** `[INH G1-FIND-61]`. Detection is mechanizable; **admission requires authority or pre-authorized policy, and no step in this chain originates a duty.** Without a named divergence condition the prospective/observed split silently tolerates exactly the case it exists to surface; without the candidate step, a detector becomes an authority.

### §E15.4.2 — Independently owned record families

**The five labels mix at least six facts with different owners, clocks and epistemic status. They are recorded separately and characterized jointly** `[KND]`. Family names and every value are `[CAN]`; the **separation** is the proposal.

| Record family | What it records | Owner | Prospective / observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `semantic_compatibility_assessments[]` | **does the revision change what the affected subject *means* for the assertions in scope** — accepted Output 3's axis ①, whose final vocabulary it routed here `[INH §E14.2.1`, `[CAN→4]`] | the semantic authority for that scope | prospective, revisable |
| `reversibility_assessments[]` | whether a **semantically valid reversal** exists for a named subject and scope — **and nothing about treatment** | the subject's owner | prospective, revisable |
| `required_treatment_determinations[]` | accepted Output 3's axis ② — **multi-valued, per affected scope** `[INH §E14.2.1`, `[CAN→4]`] | the affected scope's owner | **prospective and immutable** — see below |
| `commitment_frontier_events[]` | **discrete events**, each with kind, scope, counterparty, times and evidence (`§E15.6`) | the accountable principal | observed |
| `external_effect_executions[]` | that an effect was **emitted** at a boundary, with its `effect_id` and effect-scoped idempotency key `[INH §E13.4]` | the **emitting boundary** (GCE) | observed |
| `acknowledgement_and_reliance_observations[]` | that a counterparty **acknowledged**, or demonstrably **relied on**, the effect — **an observation about another party, not an act by OMNI** | the **observer**, admitted separately from the observation event `[INH §E13.13]` | observed |
| `domain_consequence_determinations[]` | that the effect produced a **domain-typed consequence** — clinical, financial, legal, contractual | the **affected domain owner** | observed, often much later than emission |
| `remedy_obligations[]` | that a remedy **is owed**, with the role algebra of `§E15.9.1` | the **recognizing or adjudicating authority** owns the fact *"this obligation applies"*; every other role owns its own fact — **one authoritative owner per fact, several facts** | recognized, then live |
| `remedy_capability_assessments[]` | whether a remedy pathway **exists and is usable** for a subject and scope (`§E15.4.3`) | **one attributed issuer per record.** The performer, domain or vendor being assessed is the **subject** of the assessment, not its owner; **admission of the assessment and reliance on it are separate decisions** | prospective, revisable |
| `remedy_executions[]` | what was **performed**, when, by whom, under what authority | the **executing party** | observed |
| `remedy_adequacy_determinations[]` | whether the remedy **discharged what was owed** | the **adequacy authority** of `§E15.9.1` — which is not automatically the executor and not automatically the obligor | observed, contestable |

**A family is an umbrella for reading, never an object for storing** `[KND]`. A family may group records only where **each contained record is discriminated and has one canonical fact owner in scope.** A family with two owners is the fusion the `§E15.1` splitting rule forbids, wearing a plural noun instead of a slash. **The family is not the canonical stored object; the records are.** Physicalization remains G2's.

**Two consequences for treatment determinations specifically** `[KND]`:

- **A prospective determination is immutable.** Later confirmation, execution, failure or completion is a **new record**, never a mutation of the determination — otherwise "prospective, then confirmed" is exactly the in-family mutation `CL-36` forbids.
- **Output 3's treatment values are scoped to relation-type revision, and are not universalized here.** `no_action · revalidate · remap_or_migrate · issue_new_assertions` is `§E14.2.1`'s vocabulary **for type-revision physics**. A subject contract may **adopt or specialize** it explicitly; it is not imposed on clinical performance, financial settlement, deployment or external-effect subjects, which have their own treatment physics owned by their own domains. **Forcing one treatment vocabulary across unlike subjects would be the payload-noun collapse (`D0THES-GRD-026`) at treatment grain.**

**Three separations inside those families, each of which was a fused value and is now a fact** `[KND]`:
